title: Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025
excerpt: We are thrilled to announce that fourth-year B.Pharm students Rahma Nasir, Maryam Elnazier, Naiba Khusrau, Jannat Akram, and Haneen Badreldin from Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025! Their innovative project, titled “Enhancing Healthcare Outcomes through an Advanced Pill Reminder App: A Novel Approach
content:
We are thrilled to announce that fourth-year B.Pharm students Rahma Nasir, Maryam Elnazier, Naiba Khusrau, Jannat Akram, and Haneen Badreldin from Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025!

Their innovative project, titled “Enhancing Healthcare Outcomes through an Advanced Pill Reminder App: A Novel Approach to Improving Medication Adherence and Compliance,” has garnered international recognition under the expert guidance of Prof. Aliasgar Shahiwala.

This groundbreaking app addresses a crucial challenge in medication adherence. By offering timely reminders, medication tracking, and an intuitive user interface, the app empowers patients to take their medications as prescribed, ultimately improving health outcomes.

In addition to winning the Gold Award, the team also secured an RM100 cash prize in the ‘YouTube Lucky Draw’ contest! Check out their presentation video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gerp1G185fc

The ICIIC is a prestigious platform that evaluates innovative ideas based on novelty, impact, and feasibility, and we couldn’t be prouder of our students for excelling on this global stage.

content: The Career Guidance and Alumni Office at the College of Medicine was pleased to host an insightful session titled “From Medical Student to Researcher – Your Guide to Getting Started in Research” on 22 September 2026. The session was conducted by Dr. Jumanah Mohammed, College of Medicine alumna from the Class of 2025, as part of the Office’s ongoing efforts to strengthen alumni engagement and create meaningful opportunities for students to learn from the experiences and expertise of our graduates. The session provided students with a practical introduction to the world of medical research, highlighting how they can begin developing their research skills and interests early in their medical education. Dr. Jumanah covered key aspects of getting started in research, including identifying research interests, exploring research opportunities, understanding the research process, and taking the first steps towards participating in research projects. Students also gained valuable insights into developing essential research skills and building a strong academic and research profile alongside their medical studies. The session served as a valuable platform for students to better understand the role of research in medicine and explore how early involvement in research can contribute to their academic, professional, and future career development. Through the perspective of a recent alumna, students were also able to gain relatable insights into the transition from medical student to actively engaging in research and the importance of taking initiative early in their academic journey. We extend our sincere appreciation to Dr. Jumanah, for sharing her time, expertise, and valuable insights with our students, and for encouraging them to explore research opportunities and take their first steps towards becoming future clinical researchers.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty Moderates Panel at Forbes Middle East Future Health Summit
excerpt: Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (MPharm) program at Dubai Medical University (DMU) College of Pharmacy, represented the university at the Forbes Middle East Future Health Summit, where he moderated Panel 8: “Breaking the Cycle: Rethinking Addiction Care.” The panel brought together
content:
Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (MPharm) program at Dubai Medical University (DMU) College of Pharmacy, represented the university at the Forbes Middle East Future Health Summit, where he moderated Panel 8: “Breaking the Cycle: Rethinking Addiction Care.”

The panel brought together regional experts to examine how addiction is treated across the UAE and the wider region — from the growing role of medication-assisted therapy and the pharmacist’s place within the multidisciplinary care team, to the stigma, relapse risk, and continuity-of-care gaps that often determine whether patients remain in recovery. Dr. El Ouweini guided a discussion featuring Dr. Saeed Hussein, Director of Pharmacy at a UAE rehabilitation center, and Dr. Ghattas Abu Dawoud, a clinical pharmacist practicing in addiction rehabilitation in Dubai.

Dr. El Ouweini’s participation reflected a dual role at the summit: representing DMU College of Pharmacy as faculty, and representing the Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society (ECPS), where he serves as Chairperson of the Scientific Committee. He joined fellow ECPS board members at the event, including Dr. Ghattas Abu Dawoud, ECPS Cultural Committee Chairperson and a panelist in the same session, and Dr. Khlood Catroon, ECPS General Secretary, who spoke on a separate panel addressing biosimilars and sustainable healthcare.

The summit underscored the expanding voice of clinical pharmacy in shaping healthcare policy and patient care across the region.

title: DMU Kicks Off 2026/2027 Academic Year with Groundbreaking AI Transformation in Teaching and Learning
excerpt: As Dubai Medical University (DMU) welcomes students and faculty to the 2026/2027 academic year, the University is officially launching an ambitious phase of digital transformation. Starting this Fall 2026 semester, DMU is integrating advanced AI-enabled educational tools to foster a highly interactive, student-centered learning environment. A cornerstone of this new initiative is the introduction of
content:
As Dubai Medical University (DMU) welcomes students and faculty to the 2026/2027 academic year, the University is officially launching an ambitious phase of digital transformation. Starting this Fall 2026 semester, DMU is integrating advanced AI-enabled educational tools to foster a highly interactive, student-centered learning environment.

A cornerstone of this new initiative is the introduction of the AI Student Assistant, an innovative digital companion designed to support students in their pre-class preparation. By helping learners clarify complex concepts and practice with tailored questions, the AI assistant ensures students arrive at lectures fully prepared. This technology is strategically deployed to complement, not replace, the academic expertise, mentorship, and professional judgment of DMU faculty.

This digital shift is set to significantly strengthen the university’s Flipped Classroom and Team-Based Learning (TBL) frameworks. With students mastering core materials beforehand, faculty can now dedicate valuable classroom time to higher-order application, clinical reasoning, dynamic case-based discussions, and deeper student-faculty engagement. Additionally, faculty are now equipped with AI-supported tools to refine question banks, generate authentic clinical scenarios, provide structured feedback, and analyze learning data to support student success.

To ensure a seamless transition and equip educators with the necessary skills, DMU successfully hosted a comprehensive university-wide faculty workshop on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. The full-day orientation provided practical, hands-on guidance on integrating these tools into daily instruction and assessment.

The workshop featured specialized sessions led by esteemed academic leaders:

  • Prof. Sherief Khalifa opened the event by outlining DMU’s strategic direction for the transformation of teaching and learning.
  • Prof. Hossam Hamdy delivered a thought-provoking keynote on the evolving role of educators as catalysts in the AI era in addition to hands-on implementation of Team-based Learning.
  • Dr. Shifan Khanday, Dr. Mariam Shadan, and Dr. Khaled Elmasryco-facilitated a dynamic, practical Team-Based Learning (TBL) session, guiding faculty through the hands-on application of these collaborative instructional frameworks in a classroom setting.
  • Prof. Ibrahim and Dr. Rana facilitated an actionable, hands-on session focused on the practical integration of AI into effective teaching, learning, and assessment frameworks.

The active participation and collaborative spirit displayed throughout the workshop underscore DMU’s unified commitment to educational innovation. As the new academic year begins, the university steps forward with renewed energy and a clear vision to lead the future of modern healthcare education.

This initiative reflects Dubai Medical University’s vision of advancing institutional effectiveness through innovation, automation, and data-driven quality management.

The session was led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor of Quality Assurance and Institutional
content:
The Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness (QAIE) Department at Dubai Medical University (DMU) recently organized a university-wide workshop on Mentorship and Course Registration. The initiative aimed to strengthen student support mechanisms and streamline the course registration process across all colleges.

The session was led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor of Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness, who emphasized the vital role of mentorship in guiding students throughout their academic journey. He further outlined the importance of structured course registration procedures, highlighting the need for active engagement from both students and faculty mentors to ensure academic alignment and compliance with program requirements.

Prof. Elsayed presented the multi-stage review process that governs course registration:

  • Student Course Registration – Students select courses according to their academic study plan.
  • Mentor Review and Approval – Mentors provide guidance, verify course choices, and ensure that selections are academically appropriate by reviewing the student’s assessments and transcripts.
  • College Review – The respective college validates mentor-approved course selections, ensuring consistency with academic standards and progression requirements.
  • Final Registrar Review – The Registrar’s Office conducts the final verification to confirm compliance with institutional regulations and accurate record-keeping.

The workshop underscored the significance of effective communication among students, mentors, and academic offices, ensuring that students receive the necessary academic guidance and support.

title: The QAIE Department Organizes Workshop on Digital Transformation of Meeting Minutes
excerpt: May 1, 2025 — The Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness (QAIE) Department conducted an insightful workshop introducing a new digital system for managing meeting minutes, aiming to replace the traditional documentation process with a more efficient and streamlined alternative. The workshop was led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor – QAIE, and Dr. Eslam ElNebrisi, Director
content:
May 1, 2025 — The Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness (QAIE) Department conducted an insightful workshop introducing a new digital system for managing meeting minutes, aiming to replace the traditional documentation process with a more efficient and streamlined alternative. The workshop was led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor – QAIE, and Dr. Eslam ElNebrisi, Director of QAIE.
Titled "Digital Meeting Minutes", the session addressed the pressing question, “Why change what we have now?” Participants were guided through the limitations of the current manual system and shown how the new digital platform offers significant improvements in accuracy, accessibility, and real-time collaboration.

Key advantages of the new system highlighted during the workshop included:

  • Enhanced Consistency and Standardization: Ensures uniform documentation across departments.
  • Improved Accessibility: Cloud-based access allows stakeholders to review and edit minutes anytime, from anywhere.
  • Time Efficiency: Automation features reduce manual effort, speeding up the preparation and review process.
  • Searchability and Tracking: Easy retrieval of past meeting data and tracking of action items.

Dr. Eslam, Director of QAIE, presented the second part of the session, focusing on how to submit the Policy Change Form through the portal. She also introduced the Document Bank, a centralized digital repository within the QAIE Portal, which consolidates all important records, reports, and documentation submitted by the three colleges. The Document Bank is designed to ensure standardization, streamlined access, and proper archival of institutional records for quality assurance and accreditation purposes.

title: Dubai Medical University Launches Comprehensive QAIE Portal to Drive Quality and Excellence

content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) has announced the official launch of its Quality Assurance (QA) Portal, marking a major step forward in digitizing and streamlining QA operations across the institution. This was through a workshop led by Prof. Ibrahim Elsayed, Vice Chancellor – QAIE, and Dr. Eslam ElNebrisi, Director of QAIE.

The new portal is designed to unify all QA processes into one centralized, user-friendly platform that ensures accuracy, transparency, and accessibility. Among its key features are a fully digitized policy repository, a searchable archive of old versions, and a system that allows stakeholders to suggest policy changes — which are then reviewed by relevant authorities before approval by the Deans’ Council.

In addition to policy management, the portal will support DMU’s institutional accreditation efforts, internal reviews, and reporting, while also playing a key role in research and ranking initiatives.

The QAIE team is also rolling out regular workshops to ensure all faculty and staff are trained on using the portal effectively.

title: DMU Student Represents University at Prestigious International Healthy Longevity Conference
excerpt: Dubai Medical University proudly celebrates Aena Khan, a Year 3 medical student, for representing DMU at the 3rd Healthy Longevity Conference by Nature Conferences, held at the ERTH Hotel in Abu Dhabi and hosted by Khalifa University. The global event brought together over 500 attendees and showed 91 research posters from Master’s, PhD, and undergraduate
content:
Dubai Medical University proudly celebrates Aena Khan, a Year 3 medical student, for representing DMU at the 3rd Healthy Longevity Conference by Nature Conferences, held at the ERTH Hotel in Abu Dhabi and hosted by Khalifa University.

The global event brought together over 500 attendees and showed 91 research posters from Master’s, PhD, and undergraduate students, as well as researchers from around the world. Among these outstanding contributions, Aena was selected to present her poster, supervised by Dr. Shahid Ullah Khan, titled:

“Multi-Omics Clocks in Psychiatry: Biological Aging Signatures in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) – A Literature Review.”

Aena shared that the conference was an inspiring opportunity to engage with researchers, explore innovative scientific work, and learn from renowned speakers representing institutions such as Columbia University, Stanford University, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Southern Denmark.

Her participation highlights her curiosity, commitment, and passion for advancing scientific knowledge. DMU is immensely proud of Aena for showcasing excellence, professionalism, and enthusiasm on an international platform.

title: Integrative Medicine Forum Explores the Future of Holistic Healthcare at DMU
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) participated in the Integrative Medicine International Forum, held under the theme “Path towards Integrative Medicine in Health Professions Education and Practice.” The event brought together global experts from China, India, Germany, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, showcasing how traditional healing systems and modern medicine can converge to enhance patient-centered care and
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) participated in the Integrative Medicine International Forum, held under the theme “Path towards Integrative Medicine in Health Professions Education and Practice.”

The event brought together global experts from China, India, Germany, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, showcasing how traditional healing systems and modern medicine can converge to enhance patient-centered care and promote holistic approaches in health professions education and practice.

Key speakers included:

  • Prof. Hans-Günther Machens, Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany
  • Dr. Li Huafei, UAE-licensed Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner and member of the UK Association of TCM
  • Ms. Lamia Al-Faleh, Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Humanitarian City, Saudi Arabia
  • Prof. Meera Keshavlal Bhojani, Additional Professor of Kriya Sharira (Ayurveda Physiology), All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi
  • Dr. Mariam Altheraawi, specialist in Hijama (Cupping Therapy) and Herbal Medicine

The forum featured insightful discussions on Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurveda, European Integrative Health, Rehabilitation, and Hijama, emphasizing the growing relevance of integrative medicine in modern healthcare education and research.

The event represented a milestone in advancing collaboration between diverse medical disciplines, reinforcing the shared vision of integrating holistic and evidence-based approaches for the future of healthcare.

title: DMU and Project You Collaborate to Inspire Future Innovators through “Project Nightingale”
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU), in collaboration with Project You, a social enterprise dedicated to upskilling future generations, successfully hosted “Project Nightingale”, an immersive three-day workshop designed for students from Al Salam Community School. Held from October 7–9, the program aimed to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance triage systems in emergency departments, empowering students
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU), in collaboration with Project You, a social enterprise dedicated to upskilling future generations, successfully hosted “Project Nightingale”, an immersive three-day workshop designed for students from Al Salam Community School.

Held from October 7–9, the program aimed to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance triage systems in emergency departments, empowering students to apply technology and empathy in healthcare innovation.

The workshop was led by DMU alumni Dr. Tasnima Tayb and Dr. Aisha Ismail, alongside Emergency Medicine Hive Co-chairpersons Dr. Shiza Ali and Asiya Mubeen. Over 60 students from Grades 8 and 9 participated in engaging sessions including:

  • A mock emergency simulation
  • An “Empathy Expedition” at the Dubai Medical University Hospital
  • Campus tours introducing the world of medical education
  • Design thinking workshops, culminating in a final showcase of AI-powered solutions developed with guidance from DMU mentors.

DMU expressed its appreciation to the Simulation Center—led by Prof. Basil and Dr. Marwa—and to Student Affairs for their unwavering support in bringing this initiative to life.

“Project Nightingale reflected the true spirit of mentorship, innovation, and community that defines Dubai Medical University,” the organizers shared. “We were inspired by the creativity and curiosity of Al Salam Community School’s students and grateful to Project You for this meaningful partnership.”

Special thanks were extended to the dedicated volunteer teams whose enthusiasm and commitment made the event a memorable success.

title: Aena Khan Represents DMU at MOHAP Innovation Hackathon with “SOUND” – A Breast Cancer Screening Concept
excerpt: Aena Khan, a second-year medical student at DMU, participated in the MOHAP Innovation Hackathon on March 18th, tackling the “Breast Cancer Screening & Diagnosis” challenge as part of a national initiative by the Ministry of Health and Prevention. Working alongside a diverse team of students and professionals from institutions including Khalifa University, University of Sharjah,
content:
Aena Khan, a second-year medical student at DMU, participated in the MOHAP Innovation Hackathon on March 18th, tackling the “Breast Cancer Screening & Diagnosis” challenge as part of a national initiative by the Ministry of Health and Prevention.

Working alongside a diverse team of students and professionals from institutions including Khalifa University, University of Sharjah, RAK Medical University, and NYU Abu Dhabi, Aena co-developed SOUND, Self-Operated Ultrasound Non-invasive Diagnostics, an AI-powered kiosk designed to make breast cancer screening more accessible, affordable, and private.

The kiosks guide users through a self-conducted breast ultrasound and provide instant, AI-generated preliminary results. Aena played a key leadership role in research, strategy, and pitching. SOUND stands as a promising innovation toward inclusive and early cancer detection across the UAE.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Shines at the 6th SEHA International Clinical Conference
excerpt: September 26, 2026: Dubai Medical University (DMU) College of Pharmacy took part in the 6th SEHA International Clinical Conference in Abu Dhabi, with two faculty speakers and an award-winning student poster. Clinicians, researchers, and educators from across the region and beyond attended the conference to share advances in clinical practice. Shaping the Next Generation of Clinical Pharmacists
content:
September 26, 2026: Dubai Medical University (DMU) College of Pharmacy took part in the 6th SEHA International Clinical Conference in Abu Dhabi, with two faculty speakers and an award-winning student poster. Clinicians, researchers, and educators from across the region and beyond attended the conference to share advances in clinical practice.

Shaping the Next Generation of Clinical Pharmacists

Dr. Bassam Atallah, Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs, gave a talk titled “Competency-based Clinical Pharmacy Education: Preparing Future Practice Leaders.” He described how competency-based frameworks can close the gap between academic training and real-world practice. He also explained how they prepare graduates to take on leadership roles in patient-centered, interprofessional care.

When the First-Line Vasopressor Fails

Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (MPharm) program, spoke on “Refractory Septic Shock Management: When the First-Line Vasopressor Fails.” He reviewed evidence-based strategies for patients who do not respond adequately to first-line vasopressor therapy. These included adjunctive vasopressors, corticosteroids, and other rescue options. He also highlighted the role of the critical care pharmacist in optimizing therapy at the bedside.

MPharm Student Wins Second Place in Scientific Poster Competition Ms. Shaima Moustafa, a student in DMU’s Master of Clinical Pharmacy program, won second place in the conference’s scientific poster competition. Her poster was titled “Clinical Evaluation of Adverse Effects and Tolerability of ADHD Pharmacotherapy in the Paediatric Population.” The study looks at the safety profile and tolerability of ADHD medications in children, an area of growing clinical importance. It reflects the program’s focus on research that informs safer, more effective patient care.

title: College of Medicine Students and Faculty Participate in UAE National Congress on NCDs 2026

The College of Medicine at Dubai Medical University (DMU) participated in the UAE National Congress on NCDs 2026 – From Data to Action, held on 22–23 September 2026 at the InterContinental Dubai Festival City.

The congress brought together healthcare professionals, academics, researchers, and experts to explore current approaches to the prevention, early detection, management, and long-term care of non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

The scientific program addressed a wide range of topics relevant to contemporary medical education and practice, including the UAE’s national NCD prevention strategy, diabetes and obesity, cardiovascular health, tobacco prevention, precision screening, genomics, mental health, physical activity, health literacy, patient-reported outcomes, and healthy ageing.
Further sessions explored AI and data-driven approaches to NCD prevention, early risk identification, digital health technologies, multi-omics, longevity, and the integration of prevention and screening into clinical care pathways.

The participation of College of Medicine students and faculty provided a valuable opportunity to engage with current developments in NCD prevention and management, exchange knowledge with professionals from across the healthcare sector, and strengthen the connection between medical education, research, and evolving healthcare priorities in the UAE.

The College of Medicine remains committed to providing its students and faculty with opportunities for continuous learning, professional development, and meaningful engagement with national and international healthcare initiatives.

title: College of Medicine Participates in DHA Cadaver and Human Tissue Workshop
excerpt: The College of Medicine (COM), Dubai Medical University, was represented by Dr Shifan Khanday, Dr Khaled Elmasry and Dr Sara Safwat at the Cadaver and Human Tissue Workshop organised by the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) and held at the Dubai Health Auditorium. Under the directives of the Dean of the College of Medicine, Dr Shifan
content:
The College of Medicine (COM), Dubai Medical University, was represented by Dr Shifan Khanday, Dr Khaled Elmasry and Dr Sara Safwat at the Cadaver and Human Tissue Workshop organised by the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) and held at the Dubai Health Auditorium.

Under the directives of the Dean of the College of Medicine, Dr Shifan Khanday presented the College’s cadaver-handling protocol and highlighted COM’s institutional outreach and commitment to maintaining robust policies for the ethical, safe and legally compliant management of cadavers and human tissues.

The workshop brought together representatives from key academic, healthcare and government stakeholders, including Dubai Police, the Ministry of Health and Prevention, HAYAT–The National Programme for Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation, Dubai Municipality, Dubai Airports, the Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation, Dubai Civil Aviation Authority, Dubai Knowledge, Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences, and Dubai Medical University.

The discussions will contribute to developing a workshop consensus towards a unified governance framework for the procurement, transportation, documentation, infection screening, storage, handling and dignified disposal of cadavers and human tissues. This collaborative initiative represents an important step towards strengthening regulatory alignment, institutional accountability and best practices across academic and healthcare institutions in Dubai.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty Presents Research at the 25th International Congress of the International Society for Ethnopharmacology in Italy

Dr. Saad contributed to the congress through an oral presentation entitled “Metabolomics-Guided Identification of Anticancer-Associated Metabolites in Indigofera oblongifolia and Indigofera colutea.” The study integrated UHPLC-MS metabolomic profiling, chemometric analysis, and cytotoxicity evaluation to investigate the relationship between metabolite composition and anticancer-associated activity in two Indigofera species collected from the UAE.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Showcases Outstanding Faculty and Student Achievements at the 2nd Community Pharmacy Conference
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) marked an outstanding presence at the 2nd Community Pharmacy Conference, organized by the IVPN-Network and held in Dubai on 12 September 2026. The College’s participation was distinguished by faculty leadership in the scientific program, expert presentations on contemporary pharmacy practice, and multiple awards secured by DMU
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) marked an outstanding presence at the 2nd Community Pharmacy Conference, organized by the IVPN-Network and held in Dubai on 12 September 2026. The College’s participation was distinguished by faculty leadership in the scientific program, expert presentations on contemporary pharmacy practice, and multiple awards secured by DMU faculty and students across the conference competitions.

A major highlight was the leadership role of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy at the College of Pharmacy, who served as Co-Chair of the Conference. Dr. El Ouweini also contributed to the scientific program as a speaker, addressing the important role of community pharmacists in combating antimicrobial resistance and promoting the rational use of antibiotics. His presentation highlighted the increasingly important contribution of community pharmacists to antimicrobial stewardship and responsible medication use.

Prof. Sharif Khalifa, Dean of the College of Pharmacy and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs at Dubai Medical University, also played a prominent role in the conference. He moderated the session titled “Professional Growth in Pharmacy: Core Skills, Clinical Reasoning, and New Frontiers” which brought together five speakers to explore professional development, leadership, and the evolving responsibilities of pharmacists in community practice.

Adding to the College’s scientific contributions, Dr. Bassam Atallah, Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs and Program Director for the postgraduate PharmD program at the College of Pharmacy, delivered a presentation on “Management of Dyslipidemia: Pearls for Community Pharmacists.” His session focused on practical considerations relevant to community pharmacists and their expanding role in supporting the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease.

DMU faculty and students achieved notable success in the conference’s scientific poster competition. From 30 abstracts submitted, 18 were accepted for presentation, with representatives from the College of Pharmacy earning awards across professional, postgraduate, and undergraduate categories.

Prof. Sathvik Sridhar, Professor and Chair of Pharmacy Practice Department, secured second place in the Professional Poster category. In the Postgraduate Pharmacy Poster category, DMU Master of Clinical Pharmacy Student, Basma El-Khooli, was awarded third place under the supervision of Dr. Doaa Kamal. DMU undergraduate students also distinguished themselves, with Sarah Abdel Fattah, Aya Muslih, Ranim Alrefai, and Souzan Almokdad securing second place in the Undergraduate Poster category.

The College of Pharmacy achieved further success in the conference’s Talent Show Competition, in which participants were challenged to deliver a five-minute presentation on a novel topic related to community pharmacy practice.

Among 10 participants, two College of Pharmacy students claimed the top two positions. Mariam Etri, a fifth-year pharmacy student, secured first place, while Fabina Keloth, a second-year pharmacy student, secured second place.

title: DMU – College of Pharmacy Faculty Member Represents DMU at the 6th Emirates Health Economic Society Conference
excerpt: Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (MPharm) program at Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy, represented the university as a featured speaker at the 6th Emirates Health Economic Society Conference, held on September 11th in Dubai. Dr. El Ouweini, who also serves
content:
Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Interim Program Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (MPharm) program at Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy, represented the university as a featured speaker at the 6th Emirates Health Economic Society Conference, held on September 11th in Dubai.

Dr. El Ouweini, who also serves as a Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at Dubai Medical University Hospital, took part in a clinical pharmacy session organized by the Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society (ECPS) and moderated by ECPS President Dr. Saeed Hussein. The session brought together three pillars of modern pharmacy practice: infectious disease and antibiotic optimization, presented by Dr. Waqar Ahmed (Director of Pharmacy Service and Fakeeh University Hospital); transitions of care and medication reconciliation, presented by Dr. Ghattas Abudawoud (Clinical Pharmacist at Erada Rehabilitation Center); and ICU concepts, presented by Dr. El Ouweini.

In his segment, Dr. El Ouweini addressed the evolving economic and clinical case for embedding clinical pharmacists within intensive care teams. Drawing on international, regional, and local evidence, he highlighted studies showing benefit-to-cost ratios for ICU pharmacist interventions ranging from roughly 3:1 to as high as 50:1 across health systems in Saudi Arabia, the United States, Australia, Sudan, and Europe — figures that reflect substantial cost avoidance through adverse-event prevention, individualized dose optimization, and antimicrobial stewardship. He also spoke to the leadership qualities that distinguish pharmacists who actively shape ICU decision-making from those who simply participate in rounds, and outlined the evolving skill set — spanning health economics literacy, AI-assisted clinical decision support, and prescriptive competency — that the next generation of critical care pharmacists will need.

Dr. El Ouweini, who chairs the ECPS Scientific Committee, underscored the importance of platforms such as the Emirates Health Economic Society Conference in advancing interdisciplinary collaboration and integrating pharmacists more fully into healthcare decision-making across the UAE.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Hosts Faculty Development Session on New Platform for Research and Education
excerpt: September 10, 2026, The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (COP–DMU) hosted a Faculty Development Session titled “JoVE: Accelerate Research and Education” on Thursday, 10 September 2026. The session was delivered by Dr. Ibrahim Selcuk, Director of Sales for the Middle East and North Africa at JoVE. Dr. Selcuk introduced JoVE as a video-based
content:
September 10, 2026, The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (COP–DMU) hosted a Faculty Development Session titled “JoVE: Accelerate Research and Education” on Thursday, 10 September 2026. The session was delivered by Dr. Ibrahim Selcuk, Director of Sales for the Middle East and North Africa at JoVE.

Dr. Selcuk introduced JoVE as a video-based platform for scientific research and education. He explained how peer-reviewed, step-by-step video demonstrations can help researchers master complex protocols, improve reproducibility, train laboratory members, and use time and resources more efficiently. He also outlined JoVE’s educational resources, including video textbooks and filmed demonstrations of scientific and clinical techniques.

A live demonstration showed faculty members how to search the platform, build customized playlists, create or edit quizzes, and embed videos and playlists in learning management systems. Dr. Selcuk also presented multilingual subtitles and voiceovers, downloadable article materials, and AI-supported tools that connect research literature with relevant JoVE videos.

Faculty members engaged in an interactive discussion on the availability of content in therapeutics and pharmaceutical sciences, the alignment of playlists with course outlines and reference books, and options for recommending new subject content. The discussion also highlighted the support available to help faculty integrate suitable resources into their courses and laboratory training.

title: DMU Study Highlights the Future of Pharmacist-Led Immunization in the UAE
excerpt: A newly published pilot study led by Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy provides the first published UAE evidence on patient experiences with pharmacist-administered influenza vaccination in community pharmacies. The findings were highly encouraging: 96–100% of patients reported positive satisfaction across service measures, 98% would return to a pharmacy for their next flu vaccine,
content:
A newly published pilot study led by Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy provides the first published UAE evidence on patient experiences with pharmacist-administered influenza vaccination in community pharmacies. The findings were highly encouraging: 96–100% of patients reported positive satisfaction across service measures, 98% would return to a pharmacy for their next flu vaccine, and 98% would recommend pharmacist vaccination to others.

The study also demonstrated the accessibility of community pharmacies, with 90% of patients receiving their vaccine within 15 minutes and convenience and walk-in access among the main reasons for choosing pharmacy vaccination.

These findings provide an important foundation for expanding pharmacist-led immunization beyond Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to Dubai and other Emirates. With appropriate training, licensing, and healthcare-system integration, community pharmacists could improve access to vaccination, increase public awareness and vaccine uptake, and contribute to preventing vaccine-preventable diseases. The UAE experience may also provide a valuable model for advancing pharmacy-based immunization across the Middle East and globally, and demonstrate how community pharmacists can contribute to accessible, patient-centered immunization services.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Welcomes Distinguished Pharmacy Leader Prof. Joseph T. DiPiro
excerpt: Dubai, UAE – August 24, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) was honored to welcome Professor Joseph T. DiPiro, PharmD, an internationally renowned pharmacy educator, scholar, and academic leader, for a distinguished visit focused on the evolving future of pharmacy education and practice. Professor DiPiro is Professor Emeritus and Past
content:
Dubai, UAE – August 24, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) was honored to welcome Professor Joseph T. DiPiro, PharmD, an internationally renowned pharmacy educator, scholar, and academic leader, for a distinguished visit focused on the evolving future of pharmacy education and practice.

Professor DiPiro is Professor Emeritus and Past Dean at Virginia Commonwealth University, Professor Emeritus at the University of Georgia College of Pharmacy, and Dean Emeritus at the Medical University of South Carolina. He is a former President of both the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP), and currently serves as a consultant to the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) International Services Program.

Professor DiPiro is particularly well known for his contributions to pharmacy scholarship. He served as editor of the internationally recognized textbook Pharmacotherapy: A Pathophysiologic Approach for 13 editions, as well as Editor of The American Journal of Pharmaceutical Education for 13 years. He has published more than 250 journal papers, books, book chapters, and editorials.

During his visit, Professor DiPiro met with the College of Pharmacy leadership team to discuss the current landscape of pharmacy practice in the UAE and the continued evolution of the profession globally. The discussion explored how pharmacy education can continue to evolve to prepare graduates with the knowledge, clinical competencies, technological capabilities, and professional skills needed to meet the demands of the national and global pharmacy workforce.

Professor DiPiro also toured the College’s advanced educational and research facilities, including the simulation facilities, sterile compounding laboratory, drug discovery laboratory, artificial intelligence and innovation facilities, and integrative medicine garden. The tour highlighted the College’s commitment to experiential, research-driven, and technology-enhanced pharmacy education.

A highlight of the visit was a one-hour presentation delivered by Professor DiPiro to faculty members and students, during which he shared insights from his distinguished journey in pharmacy and reflected on the transformation of pharmacy education and practice over the years.

Drawing on decades of experience, he discussed the expanding role of pharmacists, changes in pharmacy education, and some of the key challenges and barriers affecting the advancement of the profession. His presentation also addressed opportunities to further expand pharmacists’ contributions to patient care, including the importance of professional recognition and appropriate reimbursement for pharmacists’ services.

The session brought together perspectives from the United States and the evolving pharmacy landscape of the UAE, Gulf region, and wider Middle East, providing faculty members and students with valuable insights into the future direction of the profession.

Professor DiPiro’s visit provided an important platform for academic exchange and reinforced the College of Pharmacy’s commitment to engaging with international leaders, advancing innovative pharmacy education, and preparing graduates to contribute meaningfully to the evolving healthcare needs of the UAE and the global community.

The international event brought together distinguished speakers, researchers, and attendees from different countries to exchange knowledge and recent advances in pharmaceutical sciences.

Prof. Naglaa delivered a presentation entitled “Recent Advances in Marine Biota for Pharmaceutical Applications.

Her presentation highlighted the remarkable potential of marine biodiversity as a rich and still underexplored source of novel bioactive compounds and future drug candidates.

She emphasized the need for scientists to expand research on marine organisms as promising resources for drug discovery and pharmaceutical innovation.

title: College of Pharmacy Faculty Member Serves as International Faculty at ESICM Core Skills in Intensive Care Pharmacotherapy Course
excerpt: July 31, 2026 – The DMU College of Pharmacy is proud to announce that Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, was invited to serve as international faculty for the Core Skills in Intensive Care Pharmacotherapy Course, organized by the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM). content:
July 31, 2026 – The DMU College of Pharmacy is proud to announce that Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, was invited to serve as international faculty for the Core Skills in Intensive Care Pharmacotherapy Course, organized by the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM).

The intensive two-day online course brought together more than 70 healthcare professionals, including physicians, pharmacists, and nurses from across Europe and other regions of the world. The program provided participants with evidence-based updates, practical clinical insights, and multidisciplinary perspectives on the pharmacotherapeutic management of critically ill patients.

As part of the international faculty, Dr. El Ouweini contributed in two key roles. On the first day, he delivered an invited lecture titled “Glycemic Control in the ICU: Stress Hyperglycemia, Insulin Infusions, Landmark Trials, and Safe Practice,” where he reviewed the latest evidence and international guideline recommendations for managing hyperglycemia in critically ill patients. His presentation highlighted contemporary glucose targets, safe intravenous insulin infusion practices, prevention and management of hypoglycemia, and best practices for transitioning patients from intravenous to subcutaneous insulin therapy.

On the second day, Dr. El Ouweini served as a session moderator, facilitating scientific discussions and interactive learning among participants and faculty members.

Reflecting on the experience, Dr. El Ouweini stated:

“It was an honor to contribute as faculty to this outstanding ESICM educational program. The opportunity to engage with healthcare professionals from diverse backgrounds and share evidence-based approaches to critical care pharmacotherapy reinforces the importance of international collaboration in advancing patient care.”

Dubai Medical University (DMU) continues to expand its global academic partnerships through a series of high-level engagements with six leading medical institutions in India.

Professor Hossam Hamdy, Professor of Surgery and Medical Education at Dubai Medical University and an internationally recognised leader in health professions education, was invited to deliver keynote lectures and conduct academic engagements from the period July 24th – 30th 2026, at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi; Vardhman Mahavir Medical College & Safdarjung Hospital (VMMC & SJH), New Delhi; King George’s Medical University, Lucknow; JSS Academy of Higher Education & Research, Mysuru; Sri Devaraj Urs Academy of Higher Education & Research (SDUAHER), Kolar; and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Kochi.

During his visits, Professor Hamdy shared his vision on the future of health professions education in the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI), highlighting how AI is transforming medical education, clinical practice, and healthcare systems worldwide.

His presentations emphasised that AI should be viewed not merely as a technological innovation, but as a transformative force that is reshaping the entire medical education ecosystem. He discussed the need to redesign curricula, assessment strategies, faculty development, and institutional governance to prepare graduates for an AI-enabled healthcare environment while preserving the human values that remain central to medical practice, including compassion, professionalism, ethical judgement, and patient-centred care.

The academic visits also provided valuable opportunities to strengthen institutional relationships and explore future collaborations in medical education, faculty development, student training, and research. Several discussions focused on developing new partnerships and expanding existing collaborations between DMU and leading Indian medical universities, Which will allow students ad faculty exchange, collaboration in research and post-graduate studies.

These engagements reflect Dubai Medical University’s continued commitment to international collaboration, educational innovation, and the advancement of health professions education, reinforcing its position as a global partner in shaping the future of healthcare education.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Celebrates Q1 Journal Publication with Pharmacy Students
excerpt: July 9, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University congratulates a multidisciplinary research team on the publication of their study in Pharmaceutics, a Q1-ranked scientific journal. The project was led by Prof. Naglaa Shehab of the College of Pharmacy, in collaboration with Dr. Rania Shalaby of the College of Medicine, and undergraduate
content:
July 9, 2026 – The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University congratulates a multidisciplinary research team on the publication of their study in Pharmaceutics, a Q1-ranked scientific journal.

The project was led by Prof. Naglaa Shehab of the College of Pharmacy, in collaboration with Dr. Rania Shalaby of the College of Medicine, and undergraduate student researchers from the College of Pharmacy: Eslam Mahmoud Alrefaee, Fatimah Saad Altamimi, Hanaa Al-Shafea, and Naiba Khusrau.

The study evaluated the antihyperglycemic and antioxidant potential of two medicinal plants, Salacia reticulata and Caralluma tuberculata, as natural interventions for hyperglycemia. Effects were assessed in alloxan-induced diabetic female rats and benchmarked against metformin, a standard reference antidiabetic drug.

The findings underscore the therapeutic promise of these plant-based compounds and support continued phytochemical, pharmacological, and clinical research into their potential role in diabetes management.

Publication Details

“Antihyperglycemic and Antioxidant Effects of Salacia reticulata and Caralluma tuberculata in Alloxan-Induced Diabetic Female Rats”
Pharmaceutics 2026, 18(7), 785
https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18070785

content:
July 7, 2026, Dubai Medical University (DMU) has positioned itself at the forefront of integrative healthcare education, successfully concluding its Summer 2026 Herbal and Integrative Medicine Internship, a fully funded, one-of-a-kind program that drew talented students and alumni from across the UAE.

This year, DMU expanded the program’s reach beyond its own student body, welcoming students and alumni from DMU alongside six universities, including Ajman University, University of Sharjah, Gulf Medical University, University of Birmingham, RAK Medical & Health Sciences University, and United Arab Emirates University.

Delivered across two dynamic waves of 25 each, the internship brought together students and young professionals from medicine, pharmacy, nursing, and biomedical sciences. Guided by Dr. Naglaa Saad, Head of the Department of Integrative Medicine and Internship Course Leader, the program combined scientific rigor, hands-on exposure, interprofessional collaboration, and entrepreneurial skill-building.

Over a period of two weeks, participants learned directly from a distinguished faculty and practitioners, including Dr. Li Huafei (Traditional Chinese Medicine), Dr. Gerry Nastasia (Chiropractic), Dr. Shivani Sharma (Homeopathy), Dr. Yasmen Yasser (Pharmaceutical Sciences), Dr. Mariam Al Theraawi (Hijama Practitioner) and Mr. Justin Ford (Product Commercialisation Expert).

The internship’s centrepiece was its innovation project. Working in interprofessional teams, students identified unmet needs in healthcare and designed herbal health product prototypes. The program concluded in a vibrant Innovation Showcase, where teams presented to healthcare professionals and DMU leadership, with projects assessed on scientific merit, originality, branding, and market feasibility.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Conducts Faculty Development Seminar on Entrustable Professional Activities in Pharmacy Education
excerpt: 30 June, 2026, The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted a Faculty Development Seminar entitled “From Competence to Entrustment: Implementing Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) in Pharmacy Education” on 30 June 2026. The seminar was presented by Prof. Sathvik Sridhar, Professor and Head of the Department of Pharmacy Practice at DMU. It offered
content:
30 June, 2026, The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted a Faculty Development Seminar entitled “From Competence to Entrustment: Implementing Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) in Pharmacy Education” on 30 June 2026.

The seminar was presented by Prof. Sathvik Sridhar, Professor and Head of the Department of Pharmacy Practice at DMU. It offered an insightful overview of Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) and their significance in competency-based pharmacy education. The discussion highlighted how EPAs convert knowledge, skills, and professional attitudes into observable activities that students can safely execute in real-world practice settings.

The seminar underscored the use of the AACP Core EPAs as a benchmark, while also adapting them to align with UAE competency expectations, DMU outcomes, and local training needs through a phased implementation strategy.

Participants engaged in an interactive session that fostered meaningful discussion on various topics including EPA curriculum mapping, entrustment-based assessment, assessor calibration, faculty and preceptor preparation, and the utilization of evidence from OSCEs, case-based learning, skills labs, logbooks, portfolios, and experiential training. Additionally, practical pilot areas for EPAs were identified, such as patient counseling, dispensing, medication history and reconciliation, documentation, medication safety, and care plan development.

29 June, 2026, The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) conducted a Faculty Development Seminar titled “Designing Medication Safety as a System” on 29 June 2026.

title: Dubai Medical University Joins the World Stage: Ranked 401-600 Among 1,646 Universities in Times Higher Education Impact Ratings
excerpt: We are proud to share a milestone for Dubai Medical University (DMU) and everyone who has been part of our journey. This rating evaluated 1,646 universities from 116 countries based on their real-world impact toward the United Nations’
content:
We are proud to share a milestone for Dubai Medical University (DMU) and everyone who has been part of our journey.

For the first time ever, DMU has been ranked in the Times Higher Education (THE) Sustainability Impact Ratings 2026. This rating evaluated 1,646 universities from 116 countries based on their real-world impact toward the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Additionally, being ranked in the top 200 universities in the world for economic empowerment and reducing inequalities is a remarkable result for a university in just its second year of existence.

This achievement did not begin in 2025. It began in 1986, when the late Haj Saeed Bin Ahmed Al Lootah — a man who believed that education was the greatest gift a person could give to their community — founded Dubai Medical College for Girls, the first institution of medical education for women in the entire Gulf region. In 1992, he added Dubai Pharmacy College, the first of its kind in the UAE. A firm believer in the importance of education, Haj Saeed Lootah built these institutions not for profit, but for people — guided by his conviction that business and knowledge exist fundamentally to serve humanity.

Today, as Dubai Medical University steps onto the global stage for the first time, we carry his vision forward. This Rating is not just a number — it is proof that what he planted four decades ago has grown into something the world recognizes.

title: Dubai Medical University Faculty and Alumni Publish International Book Chapter on Essential Oils and Well-Being
excerpt: June 4, 2026 – Dubai Medical University (DMU) is pleased to announce the scholarly achievement of Dr. Naglaa Saad Ashmawy, Head of the Integrative Medicine Department and Assistant Dean for Quality & Accreditation, College of Pharmacy, who co-authored a book chapter with DMU alumna Ms. Jumana Haider Al-Anssari and collaborators from Ain Shams University, Egypt.
content:

The chapter, titled “Aromatic and Essential Oil Plants in Physical and Mental Well-Being,” was published by Springer Nature in the book Plant-Based Solutions for Sustainable Agriculture and Healthcare as part of the Sustainability Sciences in Asia and Africa (ADSP) series.

The chapter provides a comprehensive review of the role of essential oils and aromatic plants in promoting physical and mental well-being, highlighting their diverse pharmacological and therapeutic applications. It explores the chemistry of essential oils, their mechanisms of action, evidence supporting their health benefits, and their potential contributions to stress management, mood enhancement, cognitive function, and overall quality of life.

title: DMU’s Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini Joins Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration – Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group
excerpt: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) Program, and Chair of the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee at Dubai Medical University (DMU), as a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working
content:
Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) Program, and Chair of the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee at Dubai Medical University (DMU), as a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group under the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration (ANIC) — a milestone that strengthens the College’s growing regional footprint in interprofessional education and collaborative practice research.

ANIC — the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration — is a regional body dedicated to fostering interprofessional education and collaborative practice (IPECP) across academia and healthcare systems throughout the Arab world. The Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group serves as one of ANIC’s key sub-groups, charged with identifying priority research themes, strengthening regional research capacity, and disseminating best practices to inform policy and inspire innovation at member institutions.

The Working Group operates with three core objectives: establishing a collaborative research framework tailored to the specific IPECP needs and priorities of Arab countries; building research capacity across academic and clinical institutions through mentorship, faculty development, and joint projects; and promoting the dissemination of research findings and best practices to advance interprofessional learning at a regional and international level.As a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group, Dr. El Ouweini will contribute his expertise in clinical pharmacy practice and academic program leadership to support ANIC’s regional agenda. His work within the group will focus on identifying collaborative research opportunities, connecting academic and healthcare institutions across the Arab region, and helping build a sustainable culture of interprofessional inquiry aligned with the healthcare priorities of Arab countries.

This appointment is a natural extension of Dr. El Ouweini’s ongoing work at DMU, where he chairs the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee through its longitudinal IPE program developed in partnership with the DMU College of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing. His involvement at the ANIC level will further position DMU as a key contributor to regional IPECP dialogue and research.

The ANIC Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group has set an ambitious roadmap that includes establishing formal inter-institutional partnerships, publishing collaborative peer-reviewed research, building a regional database of IPECP collaborators, and hosting capacity-building workshops and webinars for faculty and researchers across the Arab world. The group also envisions a biannual ANIC conference and an annual IPECP newsletter as key vehicles for regional knowledge sharing.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Shines at MedEngineers 2026
excerpt: On 23 May 2026, the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) made a strong and impactful showing at MedEngineers 2026, a landmark healthcare innovation festival hosted by MedHack Global at the American University of Sharjah. The event brought together students, healthcare professionals, engineers, innovators, and members of the public from across the UAE,
content:
On 23 May 2026, the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) made a strong and impactful showing at MedEngineers 2026, a landmark healthcare innovation festival hosted by MedHack Global at the American University of Sharjah. The event brought together students, healthcare professionals, engineers, innovators, and members of the public from across the UAE, creating a vibrant platform for collaboration, creativity, and the future of healthcare. DMU was represented by three active pharmacy student clubs — the DMU-IVPN Student Club, the UAE Pharmacy Students Federation – DMU chapter (UPSF-DMU), and the Integrative Medicine Society (IMS) — alongside students who competed in the event’s flagship Hackathon competition.

MedEngineers 2026 was designed to bridge the healthcare and engineering disciplines, bringing university clubs and student societies together from institutions across the UAE to set up interactive booths, exchange ideas, and showcase student-led projects. The festival simultaneously hosted a competitive Hackathon where multidisciplinary teams of medical and engineering students worked together to design innovative solutions to real-world healthcare challenges.

The event drew participation from a diverse range of universities, including Gulf Medical University (GMU), UAE University (UAEU), Ajman University (AU), and many others, creating rich networking opportunities and meaningful dialogue about the future of healthcare across disciplines and institutions.

The DMU-IVPN Student Club, supervised by Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, represented DMU with an engaging and interactive booth, introducing visitors to the goals and initiatives of the club as well as those of the Global IVPN Network, which aims to empower healthcare professionals worldwide. The booth featured several hands-on activities designed to stimulate thinking around clinical pharmacy and healthcare technology.

In the popular “Guess the Drug” activity, participants were challenged to identify commonly used medications based on clinical scenarios. The “You Are the Pharmacist” activity invited visitors to step into a pharmacist’s role and make quick clinical decisions based on patient-specific situations. A third activity invited participants to identify healthcare technologies from provided clues — offering valuable insight into the critical importance of informatics and digital tools in modern healthcare delivery.

The Integrative Medicine Society (IMS), supervised by Dr. Naglaa Saad and Eng. Hessa Lootah, captivated visitors with a booth that elegantly blended traditional healing with modern innovation. Attendees were introduced to natural therapeutic approaches and traditional healing practices through interactive activities including a “Myth or Fact” game about medicinal herbs and a “Smell and Guess” challenge. Visitors also had the unique opportunity to create personalized herbal tea blends using peppermint, chamomile, and lavender.

A standout highlight at the IMS booth was Layla, the society’s AI-powered Integrative Medicine Assistant, which answered visitors’ questions in real time and demonstrated how technology can be harnessed to advance health education. The booth also showcased three exciting student-developed projects — EaseHer, NeuroBoost, and AyurJelly — exemplifying the creativity and entrepreneurial spirit of DMU students.

The UAE Pharmacy Students Federation – DMU Chapter (UPSF-DMU), supervised by Dr. Yasmein Yasser, also set up a vibrant interactive booth at MedEngineers 2026, engaging visitors through crossword puzzles, medication-matching exercises, clinical case scenarios, and quiz-style questions. Medical-themed prizes and rewards kept the atmosphere lively and educational, drawing visitors of all ages — from school students and parents to practicing healthcare professionals.

Through these interactions, UPSF-DMU representatives had the opportunity to discuss DMU’s programs, career pathways in pharmacy, and the value of student involvement in professional and community activities — helping to raise the profile of the pharmacy profession among a broad public audience.

Among the highlights of DMU’s participation was the outstanding performance of pharmacy student Nabiha Sadick Batcha in the MedEngineers Hackathon. Competing as part of a multidisciplinary team, Nabiha collaborated with her colleagues Nimrah Ahmer Afaq and Shams Haider from DMU’s College of Medicine, alongside Aysha Naaman AlKaabi, an engineering student from UAE University (UAEU).

Their innovative project, Smart Heal Cast, earned the team second place in the Hackathon competition. The ten finalist teams pitched their ideas to a panel of judges, with audience votes also factored into the final results. The collaborative achievement stands as a testament to the power of interdisciplinary teamwork — uniting pharmacy, medicine, and engineering expertise to address real healthcare challenges.

title: College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Research on Plant-Based Therapies for Uterine Fibroids in International Peer-Reviewed Journal
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a research article by Professor Naglaa Gamil Shehab, Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department – Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with undergraduate pharmacy students. The study was published in Pharmaceuticals (MDPI), a reputable international peer-reviewed journal, on March 23, 2026. Titled “Phytotherapeutic
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a research article by Professor Naglaa Gamil Shehab, Professor in the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department – Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with undergraduate pharmacy students. The study was published in Pharmaceuticals (MDPI), a reputable international peer-reviewed journal, on March 23, 2026.

Titled “Phytotherapeutic Intervention in Monosodium Glutamate-Induced Uterine Dysfunction: Efficacy of Lepidium sativum, Prunus armeniaca, Stachys palustris, and Solenostemma argel,” the research investigates the therapeutic potential of four medicinal plant extracts in addressing uterine fibroids — a condition that affects an estimated 70–80% of women worldwide by the age of 50 and is a leading cause of hysterectomy.

Uterine fibroids are benign tumors that significantly impact women’s reproductive health, quality of life, and fertility. Current treatment options — including hormonal therapies and surgical interventions — are often limited by high costs, side effects, and concerns about fertility preservation. This study sought to explore plant-based, cost-effective, and minimally invasive alternatives.

Using a preclinical rat model, the research team evaluated four medicinal plant extracts — Lepidium sativum (garden cress), Prunus armeniaca (apricot), Stachys palustris (marsh woundwort), and Solenostemma argel (argel) — for their antioxidant activity, hormonal modulation, and protective effects on uterine tissue. The plants were selected based on their ethnopharmacological significance in Middle Eastern, North African, and European traditional medicine, as well as emerging scientific evidence supporting their roles in reproductive health.

Key findings of the study showed that Lepidium sativum and Stachys palustris demonstrated the most significant therapeutic effects, restoring antioxidant enzyme levels (catalase, glutathione, and superoxide dismutase), reducing estrogen receptor expression, and reversing fibroid-like structural changes in uterine tissue. Solenostemma argel and Prunus armeniaca also showed promising effects through distinct antioxidant and hormonal mechanisms.

The study was co-authored by pharmacy students Fatimah Muaamar Noori, Nikoo Ali Jalali, Rodiana Mohamed Fouad Saber, and Zainab Safieldin Abdalla Mohamed — reflecting the College of Pharmacy’s dedication to nurturing the next generation of pharmaceutical scientists through hands-on research experience.

The study provides important preclinical evidence supporting the use of select plant extracts in managing fibroid-associated oxidative stress and hormonal imbalance. The authors call for further clinical research to validate these findings and translate them into effective, evidence-based therapies for women’s health.

Full article (open access):https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8247/19/3/521 DOI: 10.3390/ph19030521

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Makes History with First APhA Immunization Certification Program in the UAE
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) has marked an important milestone in pharmacy education in the United Arab Emirates by successfully organizing and delivering the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery Certificate Program — the first time this internationally accredited program has been offered by a UAE College of Pharmacy. Led
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) has marked an important milestone in pharmacy education in the United Arab Emirates by successfully organizing and delivering the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery Certificate Program — the first time this internationally accredited program has been offered by a UAE College of Pharmacy.

Led by Dr. Sahar Al-Najjar and supported by dedicated faculty members of the DMU College of Pharmacy, this pioneering program marks a transformative step in preparing the next generation of pharmacists in the UAE to serve as certified immunizers.

The APhA Immunization Delivery Certificate Program is a rigorous, multi-component curriculum recognized across the globe for its high standards in immunization training. The DMU-hosted program was structured as follows:

Self-Paced Online Theory Modules (Two Weeks):Participants completed two weeks of asynchronous, self-paced online coursework delivered directly through the APhA platform. Modules covered the immunological foundations of vaccines, the immunization schedule, vaccine storage and handling, patient screening and assessment, documentation and reporting requirements, and the management of adverse events.

Full-Day Practical Skills Training:Following successful completion of the online modules, students attended an intensive, hands-on practical training day hosted at DMU Hospital (DMUH). Under the direct supervision of qualified faculty, participants developed and refined the clinical techniques required for safe and effective vaccine administration, including injection technique, patient communication, and emergency response protocols.

Comprehensive Certification Examination:The program concluded with a comprehensive assessment comprising both a written theory examination on the APhA module content and a practical skills evaluation. Students who successfully met all requirements were formally awarded the APhA Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery certificate, recognizing them as certified immunizers.

The program was delivered to second-year students of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) program at DMU, who are currently engaged in their advanced clinical rotations. These students represent the forefront of clinical pharmacy practice in the UAE, and their certification as immunizers further equips them to contribute meaningfully to patient care and public health upon entering professional practice.

This achievement is particularly significant given the evolving regulatory landscape in the UAE. Legislation that enables pharmacist-administered immunizations is already in place, and the DMU College of Pharmacy has proactively ensured that its graduates are not only knowledgeable but formally certified and practice-ready from day one. By completing this program, the M.Pharm graduates are positioned to seamlessly assume the role of immunizers as soon as the regulatory framework is implemented across healthcare settings.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Research on Self-Medication Practices in the UAE
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a peer-reviewed research article titled “Self-Medication Practices in the UAE: Prevalence, Determinants, Public Awareness, and the Impact of an Educational Intervention on Safe Medication Use,” in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Taylor & Francis). The article is freely accessible open
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a peer-reviewed research article titled “Self-Medication Practices in the UAE: Prevalence, Determinants, Public Awareness, and the Impact of an Educational Intervention on Safe Medication Use,” in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Taylor & Francis). The article is freely accessible open access via PubMed Central (DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2600782).

The study was led by Dr. Doaa Kamal AlKhalidi, Assistant Professor in the Pharmacy Practice Department, in collaboration with co-investigator Dr. Maram O. Abbas from UAE University, and reviewed with the contribution of Dr. Shazia Jamshed from IMU, Malaysia.

Critically, the research was conducted in close partnership with a team of undergraduate pharmacy students from DMU’s College of Pharmacy:

Afnan Shebl Hamad, Khadeeja Abdulwahhab Dawood, Abir Mohamad Al Jazar, Nouran Saad Ahmed,and Menna Mohamed.

Self-medication — the use of medicines without direct medical supervision — is a common global practice that carries significant public health risks, including misdiagnosis, incorrect dosing, adverse drug reactions, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite its prevalence, evidence from the UAE on this topic had remained limited.

This community-based, cross-sectional study surveyed 400 adults across multiple UAE emirates using structured, face-to-face questionnaires, followed by a targeted educational intervention in the form of a medication safety brochure. Post-intervention feedback was then collected to evaluate changes in awareness and attitudes.

The study revealed that self-medication is highly prevalent in the UAE, with 78% of participants reporting its use within the past 12 months. Key findings include:

  • Primary drivers of self-medication: perceiving the illness as not serious (79.3%), prior medication knowledge (61.3%), and easy access to community pharmacies (42.5%).
  • Painkillers were the most frequently self-administered class of medications (88.8%).
  • Antibiotic misuse was documented in nearly one quarter of respondents — a finding with direct implications for antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
  • Over half of participants lacked awareness of drug-drug and food-drug interactions.
  • Real-life narratives shared by participants illustrated harms including pediatric dosing errors, herbal misuse during pregnancy, and delayed diagnoses due to symptom masking.
  • The educational intervention proved highly effective: 88.3% of participants reported improved understanding of self-medication risks following the brochure, and 79% expressed interest in receiving further health education from qualified healthcare professionals.

This research highlights the critical role that pharmacists, academic institutions, and public health authorities must play in promoting safe and responsible medication use. The study calls for stronger pharmacist counselling, stricter enforcement of pharmaceutical regulations — particularly around antibiotic dispensing — and the integration of targeted educational tools into community pharmacy workflows.

The publication represents a meaningful example of student-faculty collaborative research at DMU, translating classroom learning into real-world impact.

Full article available at:https://doi.org/10.1080/20523211.2025.2600782

DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2600782 | Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice, 2025

title: DMU Faculty Member Publishes Research on Natural Compounds Targeting Prostate Cancer in Leading Q1 International Journal
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a comprehensive scientific review authored by Prof. Ashraf Khalil, Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at College of Pharmacy. The review, titled “The Role of Natural Chalcones and Their Derivatives in Targeting Prostate Cancer: Recent Updates,” was published in the International Journal of Molecular
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a comprehensive scientific review authored by Prof. Ashraf Khalil, Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at College of Pharmacy. The review, titled “The Role of Natural Chalcones and Their Derivatives in Targeting Prostate Cancer: Recent Updates,” was published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences (IJMS) (Volume 26, Issue 24, 2025). IJMS is a Q1 Scopus-indexed journal and ranks among the top 10% in the fields of Chemistry and Medicinal Chemistry, reflecting the high caliber and global impact of this contribution.

Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed cancer in men worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. While hormone-based therapies offer initial benefit, a significant proportion of patients ultimately develop castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) — an aggressive, difficult-to-treat form of the disease with limited curative options.

This review focuses on chalcones — a class of naturally occurring compounds found in many plant species — and their synthetic derivatives as promising candidates for prostate cancer therapy. The review provides a thorough analysis of how both natural and synthetically derived chalcones exert anticancer activity by modulating key cellular processes, including:

  • Apoptosis (programmed cell death) induction
  • Cell cycle arrest
  • Inhibition of cancer cell migration, invasion, and metastasis
  • Suppression of angiogenesis (formation of tumor-feeding blood vessels)
  • Modulation of critical signaling pathways: PI3K/Akt/mTOR, androgen receptor signaling, and NF-κB

The review also highlights the therapeutic promise of chalcone derivatives against cancer stem cells and in overcoming resistance to conventional therapies such as taxanes and TRAIL-based treatments. A dedicated section addresses the toxicity and safety profiles of these compounds, identifying key areas for future research.

Full Article:https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/26/24/12082

title: Dubai Medical University and Emirates Health Services Host Virtual Webinar to Promote Oral Health Awareness

content:
Dubai, UAE (May 6, 2026)— In a joint effort to advance community health education, Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy, in collaboration with Emirates Health Services (EHS), recently organized a virtual webinar focused on promoting general oral health awareness across diverse age groups.

The session formed part of an ongoing community engagement and public health campaign aimed at equipping individuals with practical knowledge on maintaining oral hygiene and preventing common dental diseases. The featured speaker, Dr. Nura Jumaa, a pediatric dentist with Emirates Health Services, delivered an in-depth presentation on oral health practices tailored to different stages of life.
