She also addressed common oral health challenges affecting adolescents, adults, and the elderly, highlighting age-specific strategies for disease prevention, including proper brushing and flossing techniques, balanced nutrition, and the importance of routine dental check-ups.

A key component of the session was its focus on community engagement. Dr. Jumaa shared insights from her work in outreach programs under Emirates Health Services, where she actively promotes healthy oral health lifestyles through educational initiatives targeting families and schools. Her presentation underscored the role of public awareness in reducing the prevalence of preventable oral diseases such as dental caries and periodontal conditions.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Groundbreaking Cancer Research in International Peer-Reviewed Journal
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a significant research study by its faculty members along with students in Pharmaceuticals, a leading international peer-reviewed journal published by MDPI (Impact Factor: Q1). The article, titled “Development of Phyllanthus emblica Extract-Loaded Niosomes for Cancer Treatment: Formulation and In Vitro Evaluation,” was
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a significant research study by its faculty members along with students in Pharmaceuticals, a leading international peer-reviewed journal published by MDPI (Impact Factor: Q1). The article, titled “Development of Phyllanthus emblica Extract-Loaded Niosomes for Cancer Treatment: Formulation and In Vitro Evaluation,” was published on 6 April 2026 (Volume 19, Issue 4).

The study addresses one of the most pressing challenges in cancer pharmacotherapy: delivering plant-derived anticancer compounds effectively to tumour cells. The research team focused on Phyllanthus emblica — commonly known as amla or Indian gooseberry — a medicinal plant with well-documented anticancer, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory properties. Despite its promising therapeutic potential, amla extract suffers from poor stability and low bioavailability, limiting its clinical utility.

To overcome these barriers, the team developed an innovative niosomal drug delivery system — microscopic vesicles made from non-ionic surfactants — capable of encapsulating the amla extract and releasing it in a controlled, sustained manner.

This achievement reflects the strength of collaborative research at DMU, bringing together experienced faculty with pharmacy students:

Faculty Members:

  • Prof. Bazigha K. Abdul Rasool — Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU (Corresponding Author)
  • Dr. Al-Zahraa Khalifa — Assistant Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU
  • Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab — Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU
  • Prof. Aliasgar Shahiwala — Professor, Pharmaceutical Sciences Department, College of Pharmacy, DMU

Pharmacy Students:

  • Dema Layth Jabbar
  • Heba Marwan Ibrahim
  • Manar Ahmed Hawash
  • Maryam Jamal Afif Said

This research represents a meaningful contribution to the fields of pharmaceutical nanotechnology, drug delivery, and cancer therapy. By demonstrating that a natural plant extract can be effectively encapsulated in a biocompatible niosomal system and deliver potent anticancer effects in vitro, the team has laid a solid scientific foundation for future in vivo and translational studies.

The article is published open access and freely available at: https://doi.org/10.3390/ph19040582

title: DMU’s Prof. Sathvik B. Sridhar Delivers Expert Webinar on Renal Pharmacotherapy

Sridhar, a Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy, was invited as a Resource Person for the Clinical Pharmacy Discussion Group (CPDG) Webinar Series, organized by the Indian Pharmaceutical Association (IPA), Kerala State Branch, India. Prof. Sathvik delivered a specialised session entitled “Renal Dose Matters: Clinical Challenges
content:
DUBAI (28-04-2026) – Prof. Sathvik B. Sridhar, a Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy, was invited as a Resource Person for the Clinical Pharmacy Discussion Group (CPDG) Webinar Series, organized by the Indian Pharmaceutical Association (IPA), Kerala State Branch, India.

Prof. Sathvik delivered a specialised session entitled “Renal Dose Matters: Clinical Challenges and Practical Strategies for Pharmacists,” addressing one of the most critical areas of clinical pharmacy practice — medication management in patients with renal impairment.

The session provided an in-depth exploration of drug dosing optimisation across a range of renal conditions, including chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and patients undergoing dialysis. Participants gained practical guidance on assessing kidney function, adjusting loading and maintenance doses, understanding drug dialyzability, timing doses in relation to renal replacement therapy, and applying therapeutic drug monitoring for high-risk medications such as antibiotics, antidiabetic agents, and vancomycin.

The webinar drew a diverse audience of pharmacy academicians, clinical and hospital pharmacists, postgraduate students, and CPDG members, fostering a rich environment for professional exchange and learning.

Drawing on guideline-based principles and real-world clinical case discussions, Prof. Sathvik underscored the indispensable role pharmacists play in enhancing medication safety, preventing drug-related toxicity, and delivering patient-centred care in the context of renal dysfunction.

title: Dubai Medical University Advances Interprofessional Education with Prescribing Skills Training Program
excerpt: DUBAI (April 6, 2026) – Dubai Medical University (DMU) has successfully completed the second round of its Longitudinal Interprofessional Education (IPE) Initiative focusing on Prescribing Skills, a forward-looking program that brings together students from the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine to develop the collaborative competencies essential to modern, patient-centered healthcare practice. content:
DUBAI (April 6, 2026) – Dubai Medical University (DMU) has successfully completed the second round of its Longitudinal Interprofessional Education (IPE) Initiative focusing on Prescribing Skills, a forward-looking program that brings together students from the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine to develop the collaborative competencies essential to modern, patient-centered healthcare practice.

This latest round of the program centered on one of the most clinically significant areas of prescribing safety: Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs). Students from both colleges engaged in a rich, structured learning journey designed to build their skills in identifying, managing, and presenting ADRs — all within an interprofessional framework that mirrors real-world clinical team dynamics.

The program was delivered through a carefully designed blended format, incorporating both virtual and in-person components. Virtual sessions allowed students to prepare collaboratively and engage with foundational concepts ahead of the on-campus experience. The in-person sessions, held at DMU’s new campus, served as the culmination of this learning arc — bringing pharmacy and medical students physically together for interactive, case-based and team-based learning (TBL) exercises.

The Longitudinal IPE Initiative reflects DMU’s institutional commitment to preparing graduates who are not only technically proficient but who are equipped to function effectively as members of interprofessional healthcare teams. The program is structured to evolve across multiple rounds, progressively deepening students’ competencies in collaborative practice and prescribing skills training.

title: Dr. Sathvik Sridhar joins DMU College of Pharmacy
excerpt: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Sathvik B. Sridhar, B.Pharm, M.Pharm (Pharmacy Practice), Ph.D. (Pharmacy Practice), to the College of Pharmacy. Dr. Sathvik brings over 26 years of academic, research, and administrative experience in pharmacy education and practice, gained across India, Malaysia, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates. Dr.
content:
Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Sathvik B. Sridhar, B.Pharm, M.Pharm (Pharmacy Practice), Ph.D. (Pharmacy Practice), to the College of Pharmacy. Dr. Sathvik brings over 26 years of academic, research, and administrative experience in pharmacy education and practice, gained across India, Malaysia, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates.

Dr. Sathvik earned his B. Pharm from Bangalore University, his M. Pharm in Pharmacy Practice from JSS College of Pharmacy under Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences, and his Ph.D. in Pharmacy Practice from the same institution. In addition, he has completed specialized training in Clinical Research and Pharmacovigilance, including professional training at the Uppsala Monitoring Centre in Sweden.

Earlier in his career, Dr. Sathvik held academic and clinical appointments at the International Medical University, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and at JSS College of Pharmacy, Mysore, India, where he contributed meaningfully to clinical pharmacy education, training, and research. He has also undergone specialized training in Renal Clinical Pharmacy in Adelaide, Australia, further enriching his expertise in clinical pharmacy and specialized pharmaceutical care. His career reflects a strong blend of international, regional, and local academic experience, together with a sustained commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and academic service.

A highly accomplished scholar and mentor, Dr. Sathvik has authored over 200 peer-reviewed publications, contributed more than 20 book chapters, and published 9 books. He is also the holder of multiple international patents, including German patent certifications related to pharmaceutical innovations. His academic mentorship includes supervision of over 35 MSc theses, more than 50 undergraduate research projects, and doctoral research. In addition, he has served on advisory boards, scientific committees, and ethics and academic review bodies. His contributions to higher education and research have been recognized through several national and international honors, including the Eminent Teacher Award.

With his experience and record in teaching, scholarship, and service, Dr. Sathvik’s appointment serves to further strengthen Dubai Medical University’s mission to advance excellence in pharmacy and health professions education.

Welcome on board, Dr. Sathvik!

title: Dubai Medical University’s Research Featured in Ru’ya Magazine

DUBAI (March 23, 2026) Dubai Medical University’s research has been featured in Ru’ya Magazine, published by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MOHESR).

The research project, conducted by Dr. Naglaa Saad – Assistant Dean for Quality & Accreditation and Head of the Integrative Medicine Department, College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University, is titled “A Machine Learning Approach to Evaluating the Impact of Natural Oils on Alzheimer’s Disease Progression.” The study investigates the use of machine learning to analyze the chemical composition of natural oils and predict their potential role in slowing the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

By integrating artificial intelligence with pharmacological and natural product research, the project aims to contribute to the development of innovative therapeutic approaches for neurodegenerative diseases.

The project was a collaborative effort between Dubai Medical University (DMU) and Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT-Dubai).

title: Master of Health Professions Education Leadership Bootcamp Integrates Systems Thinking, AI and Leadership
excerpt: The College of Medicine at Dubai Medical University delivered an immersive Master of Health Professions Education Leadership Bootcamp as part of the Leadership, Change Management and Governance (HPE122) module. The bootcamp provided participants with an interactive learning experience focused on systems thinking, leadership and governance in health professions education. Moving beyond traditional lectures, the bootcamp
content:
The College of Medicine at Dubai Medical University delivered an immersive Master of Health Professions Education Leadership Bootcamp as part of the Leadership, Change Management and Governance (HPE122) module. The bootcamp provided participants with an interactive learning experience focused on systems thinking, leadership and governance in health professions education.

Moving beyond traditional lectures, the bootcamp created a dynamic environment where participants built, simulated and analyzed complex educational systems. Through hands-on engagement, participants explored how leadership decisions influence governance structures, institutional dynamics and system-level outcomes.

The sessions were led by Prof. Hossam Hamdy, a leading figure in health professions education, who guided participants through the principles of systems thinking and leadership in complex educational environments. Prof. Salah Eldin Kassab, an internationally recognized expert in medical education, facilitated discussions on governance, curriculum transformation and the dynamics of educational ecosystems.

The workshops were coordinated by Dr. Shifan Khanday, who introduced artificial intelligence as a tool to support leadership development and learning analytics. Participants also engaged in LEGO Serious Play activities, constructing models that illustrated the interconnected systems shaping educational institutions. These models demonstrated how decisions ripple across organizations.

A leadership simulation titled “HPE System Shock” further challenged participants to respond to evolving institutional scenarios while assuming roles such as dean, faculty representative and quality assurance officer. Teams adapted their models in real-time to observe how systems respond, stabilize or shift under pressure.

An AI-driven virtual dean further enhanced the experience by analyzing discussions and providing feedback on systems thinking, leadership reasoning and collaborative decision-making.

The bootcamp reflects Dubai Medical University’s continued commitment to advancing innovative approaches to medical education and preparing future healthcare educators and academic leaders.

title: College of Pharmacy’s El Ouweini Tackles Medication Management during Ramadan
excerpt: DUBAI (March 10, 2026) – Dr. Ahmed El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, at Dubai Medical University, recently delivered a regional webinar to senior pharmacy students and fresh graduates across the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMRO) of the International Pharmaceutical Students’ Federation (IPSF) Entitled “Medication Management During Ramadan,” the webinar addressed the complex clinical considerations
content:
DUBAI (March 10, 2026) – Dr. Ahmed El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, at Dubai Medical University, recently delivered a regional webinar to senior pharmacy students and fresh graduates across the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMRO) of the International Pharmaceutical Students’ Federation (IPSF)

Entitled “Medication Management During Ramadan,” the webinar addressed the complex clinical considerations involved in optimizing pharmacotherapy for patients who fast given the significant physiological, dietary, sleep, and hydration changes that occur during Ramadan. In addition, the webinar focused on medication regimens for chronic diseases that require careful adjustment to maintain therapeutic efficacy while minimizing preventable complications.

Dr. El Ouweini, who is also the Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at Dubai Medical University Hospital, provided an evidence-based framework grounded in international guidelines, including IDF-DAR and ADA recommendations, for risk stratification and individualized care planning.

The session covered comprehensive strategies for managing:

  • Diabetes, including safe adjustment of metformin, sulfonylureas, insulin regimens, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and SGLT2 inhibitors, with emphasis on preventing hypoglycemia and dehydration
  • Hypertension, focusing on optimizing long-acting antihypertensive agents, fluid balance monitoring, and patient-specific dose redistribution
  • Dyslipidemia, reinforcing the importance of continued statin therapy during fasting
  • Anticoagulation, including practical scheduling of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin monitoring considerations, and adherence counseling
  • Antibiotic therapy, with pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic considerations for time-dependent and concentration-dependent agents

The webinar also incorporated case-based clinical scenarios involving complex patients with heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and polypharmacy, allowing participants to apply medication management principles to real-world practice.

“Ramadan pharmacotherapy requires more than shifting medication timing,” Dr. El Ouweini emphasized during the session. “It demands structured risk assessment, individualized therapeutic planning, close monitoring, and proactive patient education to ensure safety without compromising clinical outcomes.”

The interactive session was met with strong engagement from participants across the EMRO region, highlighting the growing interest among emerging pharmacists in culturally competent, patient-centered care.

content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) continues to lead transformative advancements in medical education through the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within a robust Interprofessional Education (IPE) framework.

Dubai Medical University has embedded AI-powered learning tools into a structured interprofessional model where medical, pharmacy, and nursing students learn with, from, and about one another. This approach ensures that technological advancement is complemented by meaningful collaboration across healthcare disciplines.

Through AI-driven clinical simulations and team-based training exercises, students engage in realistic, data-informed clinical scenarios that enhance diagnostic reasoning, therapeutic decision-making, and patient management skills. Pharmacy students, in particular, benefit from exposure to interdisciplinary case discussions that strengthen their role in medication therapy management, safety optimization, and collaborative care planning.

The integration of AI-enhanced simulations supports the development of critical thinking, effective communication, and coordinated clinical practice — competencies essential for delivering high-quality, patient-centered healthcare.

This milestone project was successfully implemented through the dedicated efforts of Dr. Naglaa Saad Ashmawy and Eng. Hessa Lootah, whose leadership and commitment were instrumental in bringing the initiative to life for the DMU community.

The impact of DMU’s forward-thinking educational model has attracted international attention. Reuters recently visited the DMU campus to highlight the University’s pioneering approach, showcasing how AI integration within interprofessional education is shaping the future of healthcare training.

title: DMU College of Medicine Students Shine at WHX General Surgery Conference.
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly celebrates the outstanding participation of College of Medicine students at the prestigious WHX General Surgery Conference, where academic excellence, innovation, and research leadership were prominently showcased. A total of 10 DMU medical students presented their research, reflecting the university’s strong commitment to student-led scholarly activity and evidence-based clinical learning. The
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly celebrates the outstanding participation of College of Medicine students at the prestigious WHX General Surgery Conference, where academic excellence, innovation, and research leadership were prominently showcased.

A total of 10 DMU medical students presented their research, reflecting the university’s strong commitment to student-led scholarly activity and evidence-based clinical learning. The presentations covered a diverse range of contemporary and clinically relevant topics, including:

  1. Lessons from a Rare Case of Klippel-Trénaunay Syndrome: Case Report and Review by Afra Al Darmaki
  2. Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor with Low Mitotic Activity and KIT Exon 11 Mutation: A Case Report by Fatma Badr Alzarooni, Sarah Ali Alyammahi and Shouq Abdulwahed
  3. Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute Appendicitis: Evaluating the Role and Limitations of Clinical Assessment Versus Imaging by Lian Wathek Arabi Katbi,
  4. Holographic Imaging in the Operating Room: Exploring New Visualization Technologies by Dalia Diary Abdulrahman, Aycha Sleiman Zaher, Laweezah Arif Zulquarnain, Fathima Samreen
  5. AI-Enabled Wound Assessment in Surgical Practice: Current Capabilities and Future Directions by Fatima Aljaziri
  6. The Acute Abdomen : A Diagnostic and Management Algorithm for Students by Faaizah Ahmed, Fathimathul Henna, Sadhana Parveen, Saniya Merchant, Naya Almikhi
  7. Spontaneous Congenital Transmesenteric Internal Hernia in an Adult Without Prior Abdominal Surgery: A Rare Cause of Acute Small Bowel Obstruction by Sana Ahmed, Laian Mohamad Hamod,Leen Ibrahim Sabbagh,Rokia Malahifci, Maryam Munzer Manzalgi.
  8. A Cross-Sectional Study on Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Toward GLP-1 Agonists in UAE Adults: Implications for Obesity and Diabetes Management by Sarah Ali Alyammahi

The student research projects were conducted under the academic supervision and mentorship of Dr. Shifan Khanday, Associate Dean of Research and Graduate Studies, and Prof. Yousef El Tayeb, Dean of College of Medicine ,whose guidance played a key role in strengthening the scientific quality and clinical relevance of the work.

The scientific session was further distinguished by the leadership of Dr. Ali Khamas, who served as the Session Chair, facilitating scholarly discussions and providing expert insights during the presentations.

This achievement reflects DMU’s strategic focus on:

  • Early integration of research into undergraduate medical education
  • Encouraging innovation in surgery and digital health
  • Developing future clinician-scientists equipped to address emerging healthcare challenges

The active participation of DMU students at an international platform such as WHX highlights the university’s growing impact in academic medicine and reinforces its mission to foster a culture of research, innovation, and global engagement.

Dubai Medical University congratulates its students and faculty mentors for this remarkable achievement and their contribution to advancing surgical science and medical innovation

title: From Curriculum to Competency: DMU’s Engagement in Global Health Professions Education
excerpt: On February 4–5, Dr. Arina Ziganshina represented the College of Medicine (COM), Dubai Medical University, at the First International Higher Education Conference on Health Professions Education held in Muscat, Oman. Dr. Arina had the privilege of chairing an oral presentation session within the Technology-Assisted Learning and Assessment track. The session featured presentations on a range of innovative
content:
On February 4–5, Dr. Arina Ziganshina represented the College of Medicine (COM), Dubai Medical University, at the First International Higher Education Conference on Health Professions Education held in Muscat, Oman.

Dr. Arina had the privilege of chairing an oral presentation session within the Technology-Assisted Learning and Assessment track. The session featured presentations on a range of innovative topics, including the use of artificial intelligence in teaching and assessment, learning anatomy through digital anatomical models, simulation-based pharmacology training activities, and research on the impact of virtual reality on physician competency development.

In addition, Dr. Arina presented COM’s journey in adapting assessment strategies to evaluate EmiratesMEDs competencies within an evolving medical curriculum. Her presentation was delivered in the Assessment track, chaired by internationally renowned Professor John Norcini. Many presentations within this track focused on experiences in evaluating Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) in postgraduate programs. A consensus emerged among session participants on the value of frequent testing for learning, even when used solely for formative purposes. Professor Norcini emphasized that the most effective approach is the establishment of a holistic assessment system, ensuring coherence across courses and academic years and avoiding gaps in competency assessment.

The conference plenary sessions delivered powerful messages to educators from the MENA region, highlighting that the primary mission of health professions education is to improve patient outcomes. To achieve this goal, universities must actively engage stakeholders and industry partners in educational design and delivery, integrate community engagement and interprofessional learning activities into curricula, and contribute to creating supportive workplace environments for healthcare professionals.

Extensive discussions addressed the role of artificial intelligence in education and clinical practice, particularly its potential to support professors and physicians in their professional tasks. However, educational psychologist Professor Janet Grant cautioned policymakers about the potential deskilling effects of AI. She advocated for its cautious and justified use by both faculty and students to ensure the development of robust cognitive skills and clinical reasoning. Ultimately, health professionals must possess sufficient subject-matter expertise to critically evaluate information and identify AI-generated inaccuracies or hallucinations.

Dr. Arina sincerely thanks the Dubai Medical University leadership for their support and encouragement to participate in international educational conferences, enabling continuous learning and the sharing of the University’s experience on a global platform.

title: Dubai Medical University Hospital Hosted Certificate of Competence Ceremony in Health Professions Education in Dubai

content:
Dubai Medical University Hospital hosted the Certificate Distribution Ceremony on January 9, 2026, recognizing health professionals who successfully completed the Certificate of Competence in Health Professions Education (HPE). The program was delivered by Professor Hossam Hamdy, Professor of Surgery and Medical Education, and Professor Salah Eldin Kassab, Associate Dean for Academic Affairs and Program Director of the Master of Science in Health Professions Education, College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University.

The ceremony marked the completion of an intensive 40-contact-hour professional development program designed to prepare clinicians for their educational roles within Dubai Medical University’s integrated Academic Health System, reflecting the strong partnership between the University and its teaching hospital.

The event brought together physicians, nurses, allied health professionals, senior faculty, and institutional leaders, highlighting the strength of the academic–clinical partnership that underpins the Academic Health System. Participants were recognized for their commitment to excellence in teaching and learning, assessment practices, and curriculum design competencies.

The presence of Dubai Medical University leadership, including Professor Sherief Khalifa, Vice Chancellor for Academics Affairs and Dean of the College of Pharmacy; Professor Yousif El-Tayeb, Dean of the College of Medicine; and Professor Basil Amarneh, Dean of the College of Nursing, together with hospital leadership, underscored the strategic importance of this initiative in strengthening the Academic Health System. By equipping clinicians with advanced educational competencies, the program supports enhanced clinical training and safer, more effective patient care.

This ceremony reflects Dubai Medical University’s ongoing commitment to continuous professional development, academic excellence, and the integration of education and clinical service. Through initiatives such as the Certificate of Competence in Health Professions Education, the University continues to empower healthcare professionals in their dual roles as clinicians and educators, fostering innovation and excellence across its Academic Health System.

title: Conference visits to Indonesia and China-Dr Shahid
excerpt: Dr. Shahid Ullah Khan (Dr. SK) recently concluded a highly successful international academic visit to Sanya China and Semarang Indonesia from 27 November to 7 December 2025, where he was invited as a distinguished speaker at multiple scientific and academic forums. During this visit, Dr. Khan delivered a series of impactful talks under the themes:
content:
Dr. Shahid Ullah Khan (Dr. SK) recently concluded a highly successful international academic visit to Sanya China and Semarang Indonesia from 27 November to 7 December 2025, where he was invited as a distinguished speaker at multiple scientific and academic forums.

During this visit, Dr. Khan delivered a series of impactful talks under the themes: “The Beauty of Nanotechnology in Nanomedicine (with special focus on Triple-Negative Breast Cancer),” “From Kick-Start to Refinement: How to Write a Scientific Paper,” and “Nanotechnology as a Cutting-Edge Bridge Technology for Livestock.” His lectures were well received by faculty members, researchers, and international students, sparking vibrant discussions on innovation, research translation, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

In Indonesia, Dr. Khan also visited a leading Cancer and Stem Cell Research Center, where he engaged in in-depth scientific exchanges with renowned researchers and scientists from Japan, South Korea, MIT (USA), Thailand, and other countries. These interactions led to the sharing of novel ideas and invitations for future international collaborations.

The visit further provided valuable scientific insights in China, with promising discussions toward initiating new collaborative projects focused on the early detection of breast cancer using multi-omics approaches.

Reflecting on the journey, Dr. Khan described it as a truly memorable experience, enriched by meaningful academic exchange and the enthusiasm of international students. He expressed gratitude for the warm hospitality, productive discussions, and the wonderful moments captured throughout this inspiring academic tour.

Dr. Shahid Ullah Khan sincerely expresses his gratitude for the generous financial and institutional support provided by Dubai Medical University (DMU). He is especially thankful to the Research Associate Dean, the Dean of the College of Medicine, and the Vice Chancellor (Academic), DMU, whose encouragement and support made this international academic engagement possible. Their continued commitment to advancing research excellence and global collaboration is deeply appreciated.

title: DMU Strengthens Global Footprint at SHARE 2025, Delivering Key Talk on Ethics of Internet of Bodies in UAE
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) marked a significant milestone on 19 November 2025 by participating in the SHARE 2025 conference hosted by Monash University in Australia. The SHARE (Sharing about Healthcare Artificial intelligence Regionally) conference is designed to unite clinicians, technologists and researchers across the Indo-Pacific region, facilitating the exchange of pioneering digital health projects and
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) marked a significant milestone on 19 November 2025 by participating in the SHARE 2025 conference hosted by Monash University in Australia. The SHARE (Sharing about Healthcare Artificial intelligence Regionally) conference is designed to unite clinicians, technologists and researchers across the Indo-Pacific region, facilitating the exchange of pioneering digital health projects and applied AI in healthcare.

DMU was represented by Dr Shifan Khanday, Acting Associate Dean of Research and Head of the AI & Smart Education Unit. Dr Khanday delivered a compelling presentation titled:

“Governing the Bio-Connected Future: Ethical Framework for Internet of Bodies Technologies in the UAE.”

Her talk illuminated the pressing implications of emerging connected-body technologies for frontline healthcare professionals — especially regarding data privacy, patient autonomy, and clinical decision-support. It also spotlighted the experiences of labour and migrant-worker communities in the UAE, who often face challenges around digital literacy, access, affordability and informed consent. These insights underscored the imperative for equitable, culturally sensitive and ethically governed technology ecosystems in future healthcare systems.

By contributing to this high-level international forum, DMU reinforced its growing global presence and leadership in advancing ethical discourse, emerging technology integration, and the future of health-professions education.

content:
Dubai, UAE — October 2025
Innovation met intelligence as Dr. Shifan Khanday, Acting Associate Dean of Research and Head of the AI and Smart Education Unit at Dubai Medical University (DMU), delivered a captivating workshop titled “Agentic AI in Content Creation: The Rise of Virtual Avatars.”

In a session that blended science, imagination, and ethics, Dr.Shifan introduced participants to the next evolution of AI—Agentic AI, where machines don’t just respond but reason, act, and adapt. Through interactive live demos and creative group activities, attendees explored how AI avatars can teach, emote, and collaborate—bridging empathy and technology in powerful new ways.
Participants designed their own AI avatar educators, discussed ethics and autonomy, and reflected on how “AI won’t replace educators, but educators using AI will transform education.”

Closing with a live survey on Bio-connectivity ,Cybersoma and the Internet of Bodies, the session left attendees inspired—seeing a future where education becomes truly alive, responsive, and human-centered.

DMU continues to lead the UAE’s educational innovation frontier—where technology meets imagination, and learning becomes limitless

content:
Dr. Youness Zidoun, Director of the Simulation Center, was recently invited to speak at the prestigious 7th Zhujiang Development Forum on Simulation in Healthcare, held in Guangzhou, China. The forum brought together leaders, educators, and innovators from across Asia and beyond to advance dialogue and share best practices in clinical simulation.

Dr. Zidoun delivered two keynote sessions during the event. His first, presented at the Forum of Directors, was titled:

“Designing Excellence: The Strategic Development of Clinical Simulation Centers.”

In this session, he outlined strategic frameworks for developing high-impact simulation centers, emphasizing leadership models, infrastructure planning, and long-term sustainability.

His second keynote, delivered during the Plenary Session, was entitled:

“The AI Paradox in Healthcare: Understanding the Lag in Medical Education.”

His presentation examined the growing divide between the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and the pace of curricular integration in health professions education. Dr. Zidoun offered insights into responsible implementation and the need for urgent upskilling of academic faculty.

“It was a privilege to contribute to such a forward-thinking forum,” Dr. Zidoun noted. “The energy, commitment, and vision emerging from China’s healthcare simulation community is truly inspiring.”

The participation highlights our institution’s growing global engagement and leadership in the field of health simulation and medical education innovation.

title: Dubai Medical University shares expertise in International Webinar on Strengthening Integrity and Reliability in Digital Assessments

content:
On June 10, Dr. Arina Ziganshina, Head of the Examination and Assessment Unit at Dubai Medical University (DMU), participated as a panelist in an international webinar titled “Strengthening Assessments – Ensuring Integrity and Reliability in High-Stakes Digital Exams,” hosted by Turnitin.

Drawing from DMU’s extensive experience in digital assessment, Dr. Arina shared practical insights into the advantages of technology-enhanced evaluations. She highlighted key benefits such as fostering academic integrity, reducing faculty workload, and generating valuable data that supports multiple educational and institutional objectives.

Dr. Arina emphasized that the successful integration of digital technologies in examinations requires a strong foundation, including comprehensive user orientation, expert technical supervision, and continuous evaluation and improvement. She also outlined how DMU has adapted its policies and procedures to align with advances in digital assessments.

During the webinar, Dr. Arina offered valuable strategies for integrating technology into performance-based assessments and assignments. She also showcased how data generated by examination software is used at DMU to benefit students, faculty, and university leadership—through item analysis, student feedback, educational process evaluation, KPI monitoring, and mentoring within a competency-based education framework.

DMU takes pride in being a fully digital assessment institution, equipped with the infrastructure, expertise, and commitment to quality needed to lead and share best practices across the global education community.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Medical Education: Adaptability, AI, and Accreditation
excerpt: On May 25-28 Dr. Arina Ziganshina attended World Federation for Medical Education world conference 2025 in Bangkok, Thailand. Most sessions were related to the future of Medical Education. Wide accessibility of data and AI tools might change the role of physicians to patient guides in the world of information. Patients in turn must be more and more involved
content:
On May 25-28 Dr. Arina Ziganshinaattended World Federation for Medical Education world conference 2025 in Bangkok, Thailand. Most sessions were related to the future of Medical Education. Wide accessibility of data and AI tools might change the role of physicians to patient guides in the world of information. Patients in turn must be more and more involved and engaged in decision making regarding their health. A lot was said regarding the importance of cultural awareness in medicine since the world is getting more and more global. An eye-opening workshop related to system-based practice emphasized the requirement for early application of health systems knowledge by medical trainees. It also highlighted the demands for strong collaboration skills in doctors as well as for interdisciplinary education opportunities unifying relevant medical and non-medical professionals. Doctors must also clearly understand how AI works and become friends with technologies. The only way for both educators and doctors to meet these expectations is to be adaptable continuous learners.

In assessment track the educators from all over the world discussed how to reduce bias in grading, listed the factors affecting feedback quality, compared the quality of assessments produced by faculty vs AI and engaged in the debate whether programmatic assessment appears to be feasible. Dr. Arina Ziganshina in turn introduced international colleagues to customized competency centered assessment system at DMU College of Medicine. The title of her work is Contextualized programmatic assessment system for the EmiratesMEDs Competency Framework: The Case Study. The presentation initiated rich discussion and received very positive feedback from the audience.

Since the conference was hosted by WFME the sessions addressing accreditation of medical programs were highly demanded. As a conclusion, the experts agreed that despite high cost and resource investment, institutional accreditation is important and highly beneficial. For instance, it is known to improve educational climate, attract better applicants, increase achievement of learning outcomes, promotes innovation, fosters continuous quality improvement, and even elevates satisfaction of all stakeholders of the educational process.

Finally, conference participants discovered the complexity of identity of a medical teacher. There is no doubt that any ways of faculty development are important, but in addition to the availability of relevant programs and activities institutional support is what really matters. With this said Dr. Arina sincerely thanks College of Medicine and DMU leadership for providing her with an opportunity to learn, network and represent the university in such an insightful educational event.

title: Dubai Medical University at the Forefront: Exploring Ethical AI in Education with Turnitin

While AI-focused conferences are becoming more frequent, Dr. Arina appreciated how this session brought fresh and practical insights
content:
On May 21st, Dr. Arina Ziganshina had the honor of representing Dubai Medical University (DMU) at a workshop and roundtable discussion hosted by Turnitin. The event stood out for its exceptional participants, engaging activities, and thoughtful venue.

While AI-focused conferences are becoming more frequent, Dr. Arina appreciated how this session brought fresh and practical insights into the ethical application of artificial intelligence in education.

Key takeaways:

  • Ethical AI starts with faculty as role models for integrity and responsibility.
  • Assessment should focus on the learning process rather than the final product—students must understand the "why" behind assignments, and faculty should explore the "how" behind students’ work.

Dr. Arina left the event inspired and ready to implement these perspectives within DMU’s academic framework.

title: Global Impact Grants awarded – Advance HE

content:
We are delighted to announce 15 awards under our 2024-25 Global Impact Grants programme to support international member institutions in sharing good practice in higher education.

The grants were awarded from a large and competitive field and will allow the winners to develop case studies showcasing successful higher education initiatives that have demonstrated meaningful impact on students and staff.

Applications were made under four themes that our members regard as key challenges in higher education: Leading and Governing Transformation, Protecting Inclusion in Times of Change, Securing Student Outcomes, and Designing Education for the Future.

The awardees, by category, are:

Securing student outcomes
  • Deakin University, Australia – ‘Coffee Conversations at Deakin – A Relationship-Rich Approach to Student Success’,Cassandra Iannucci
  • Nazarbayev University, Kazakhstan – ‘Enhancing Student Outcomes through Integrated Career Development Initiatives’,Gaini Yessembekova
  • RMIT, Vietnam – ‘From Exam Halls to Hackathons: Authentic Learning Through Competitive Assessment in Software Engineering’,Tom Huynh
  • National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan – ‘Creativity in SDGs Action: Empowering Student Sustainability through Competition-Based Learning’, Dr Sirirat Sae Lim
  • The University of Queensland, Australia – ‘Across the student lifecycle’ ,Renee de Simone & The Young Achievers Program
  • University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR – ‘Developing tomorrow’s global healthcare professionals: Integrating leadership skills in the undergraduate curriculum’, Prof. Fred Ganoce & Jannie Roed
Governing and leading transformation

  • University of Newcastle, Australia – ‘Future Pedagogy in Action: Engaging Gen Z in Experiential Digital Learning for Sustainable Futures’,Tamara Young
  • University of Kurdistan Hêwler, Iraq – ‘Reimagining Assessment: A Modern Approach to Student Evaluation’,Tarik A. Rashid & Hussein M. Ali

title: Dubai Medical University Announces Dr. Shifan Khanday’s Nomination for the UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of ICT in Education
excerpt: Dubai Medical University is proud to announce that Dr. Shifan Khanday, Associate Dean of Research(Acting) and Head of the AI and Smart Education Unit, has been officially nominated by the UAE National Commission for the prestigious UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in Education). content:
Dubai Medical University is proud to announce that Dr. Shifan Khanday, Associate Dean of Research(Acting) and Head of the AI and Smart Education Unit, has been officially nominated by the UAE National Commission for the prestigious UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in Education).

The UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize, established in 2005 and funded by the Government of the Kingdom of Bahrain, honors two global laureates each year for outstanding achievements in the application of ICT to improve teaching, learning, and education performance. Laureates are selected by the Director-General of UNESCO based on the recommendation of an independent international jury of experts, and eac receives a monetary award of USD 25,000 along with a diploma during the award ceremony at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris.

Vice Chancellor Academic’s Prof Sherief Khalifa commented that Dr Shifans nomination not only affirms her personal dedication to educational innovation but also reflects Dubai Medical University’s ongoing commitment to excellence, leadership, and transformation in the field of digital and AI-powered education.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Dr. Shifan Khanday for this significant achievement. Her work continues to inspire a new generation of learners and educators, driving forward Dubai Medical University’s mission to shape the future of education through innovation.

The final announcement of the UNESCO Prize laureates will be made later this year.

title: Dubai Medical University Launches Longitudinal Interprofessional Prescribing Skills Training Program
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly announces the launch of a comprehensive longitudinal training program in Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA), developed collaboratively by the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine. This pioneering initiative reflects the University’s commitment to advancing patient safety, interprofessional education, and practice-readiness among near-to-graduate healthcare students. The Prescribing Skills Assessment is
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly announces the launch of a comprehensive longitudinal training program in Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA), developed collaboratively by the College of Pharmacy and the College of Medicine. This pioneering initiative reflects the University’s commitment to advancing patient safety, interprofessional education, and practice-readiness among near-to-graduate healthcare students.

The Prescribing Skills Assessment is designed to rigorously evaluate and strengthen students’ competencies in safe and effective prescribing. The assessment framework encompasses multiple critical domains, including:

  • Safe and rational prescribing
  • Prescription review and validation
  • Identification and management of adverse drug reactions
  • Therapeutic planning and clinical management
  • Laboratory and diagnostic data interpretation
  • Pharmaceutical calculations
  • Therapeutic drug monitoring
  • Patient communication and counseling

The program is structured as a longitudinal curriculum model beginning in Year 2 and continuing through Year 5. It progressively builds prescribing competence from foundational principles to advanced clinical application during experiential and clinical training. The initiative is fully integrated across courses within the curriculum, ensuring continuous reinforcement of prescribing competencies in both theoretical and clinical contexts.

This collaboration is particularly timely. While medical graduates are already licensed prescribers, pharmacy prescribing authority is anticipated to be introduced in the United Arab Emirates soon for selected minor ailments. By proactively preparing pharmacy graduates for this expanded scope of practice, DMU is positioning its students at the forefront of evolving healthcare delivery models in the region.

The integration is led by the College of Pharmacy under the supervision of Dr. Riza Assadi and Dr. Ahmad El-Ouweini, in close collaboration with the College of Medicine, represented by Prof. Nevien Hendawy and Dr. Rania Shalaby. This intercollege leadership exemplifies DMU’s commitment to interprofessional education (IPE) and collaborative practice.

The inaugural session of the program focused on pharmaceutical calculations, an essential foundation for safe prescribing. Students from both the College of Medicine and the College of Pharmacy participated in an interprofessional training workshop, working collaboratively in mixed groups to solve clinically oriented calculation cases. The session emphasized teamwork, shared clinical reasoning, and mutual understanding of professional roles in medication safety.

This initiative marks a significant milestone in curriculum innovation at Dubai Medical University. By embedding prescribing skills training longitudinally and interprofessionally, DMU ensures that its graduates are equipped not only with knowledge, but with the practical competence, clinical judgment, and collaborative mindset required for safe prescribing practice. The University looks forward to expanding the application of this program across additional courses and clinical experiences, further strengthening prescribing readiness and advancing excellence in healthcare education.

title: DMU MPharm Graduate Releases Research in Q2 Scopus-Indexed Journal
excerpt: DUBAI (March 11, 2026) – Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy announces the publication of a research article authored by Ms. Zainab Almardod, a recent graduate of the Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, in the Q2, Scopus-indexed journal Critical Care Research and Practice. The article, titled “Prevalence, Risk Factors, Characteristics, and Clinical
content:
DUBAI (March 11, 2026) – Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy announces the publication of a research article authored by Ms. Zainab Almardod, a recent graduate of the Master of Pharmacy (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, in the Q2, Scopus-indexed journal Critical Care Research and Practice.

The article, titled “Prevalence, Risk Factors, Characteristics, and Clinical Outcomes of Thrombocytopenia in the Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study”, was conducted under the supervision of Prof. Kishore Gnana Sam, a Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the college.

This prospective cohort study enrolled 276 critically ill patients in a tertiary intensive care unit and investigated the epidemiology and clinical impact of thrombocytopenia. The study reported a prevalence of 38.8% and an incidence of new-onset thrombocytopenia of 22.5%. Importantly, new-onset thrombocytopenia was found to be independently associated with major bleeding and increased ICU mortality. The research also identified key predictors, including shock, sepsis, and renal impairment, and highlighted medication-related factors associated with severe thrombocytopenia.

The study contributes valuable epidemiological data from the Gulf region, where ICU-related thrombocytopenia has been underrepresented in the literature. Its findings provide clinically relevant insights that may support improved risk stratification, monitoring, and management strategies in critical care settings.

This publication reflects the strong research component embedded within the MPharm (Clinical Pharmacy Specialization) program, which emphasizes methodological rigor, advanced statistical analysis, and clinically meaningful outcomes. It also demonstrates the college’s commitment to cultivating postgraduate students capable of producing high-quality, practice-oriented research that contributes to evidence-based patient care.

The conference was also attended by faculty and students from the DMU College of Pharmacy and College of Nursing, reflecting the university’s strong engagement in academic, clinical, and professional development activities in the field of cardiovascular health.

title: College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University Demonstrates Strong Engagement in the 9th Regional Workshop on Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) demonstrated strong academic engagement and leadership through active participation in the 9th Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop, entitled “Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education.” The two-day workshop was held on January 16–17, 2026, at Ajman University – College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences, in partnership with the
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) demonstrated strong academic engagement and leadership through active participation in the 9th Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop, entitled “Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education.” The two-day workshop was held on January 16–17, 2026, at Ajman University – College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences, in partnership with the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP), The Commission for Academic Accreditation (CAA), and the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MOHESR)

Faculty members from both the Pharmacy Practice and Pharmaceutical Sciences Departments at DMU attended the workshop, which brought together educators and leaders from across the region and internationally. The event featured impactful dialogue, collaborative learning, and hands-on activities focused on the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) in pharmacy education. Sessions addressed ethical principles, personalized learning, assessment analytics, clinical education, administrative efficiency, and legal and regulatory considerations, delivered by distinguished speakers from ACPE and leading pharmacy schools in the United States.

In addition to participation, DMU faculty made notable scholarly contributions to the workshop:

  • Dr. Naglaa Saad, Assistant Dean for Quality and Accreditation, College of Pharmacy, DMU, delivered an oral presentation titled “AI-Driven CQI Intelligence Hub: A Model for Transforming Assessment Analytics.” Her presentation showcased an innovative and ethical framework that leverages artificial intelligence to integrate multi-modal assessment data and generate actionable insights for continuous quality improvement (CQI). The model emphasized the responsible use of AI to enhance faculty decision-making while maintaining academic oversight, data integrity, and accreditation readiness.
  • Dr. Rana Sammour, Associate Dean for Academic Affairs, DMU College of Pharmacy, presented a poster entitled “Enhancing Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes: A Showcase of Interactive Learning in Pharmacy Education.” The poster highlighted DMU’s experience in transitioning from traditional lecture-based teaching to interactive and technology-enhanced strategies, including the use of digital and AI-driven tools, and demonstrated their positive impact on student engagement and learning outcomes in undergraduate pharmacy courses.
  • Dr. Hanan Anbar, Associate Dean for Research, DMU College of Pharmacy, presented a poster focusing on the role of artificial intelligence in pharmacy education and research, with particular emphasis on effective and ethical integration. Her work explored AI applications for instructors and students—such as personalized learning, assessment, feedback, and virtual tutoring—as well as research-related uses including literature review, manuscript editing, and grant-writing support. The poster also addressed opportunities, risks, and key challenges, underscoring the importance of clear ethical boundaries and responsible AI use.

DMU’s active involvement in this regional workshop reflects the College of Pharmacy’s continued commitment to educational innovation, quality assurance, and responsible integration of emerging technologies.

title: DMU’s Prof. Mirza Baig Speaks at The International Conference on “Avenues and Opportunities in Pharmaceutical Research and Practice
excerpt: Professor Mirza R. Baig, Program Director for the Master of Clinical Pharmacy and Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), was invited as a speaker at an international conference organized by Indira University, Pune, India, held on 13–14 January 2026. During the conference, he delivered an insightful and
content:
Professor Mirza R. Baig, Program Director for the Master of Clinical Pharmacy and Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), was invited as a speaker at an international conference organized by Indira University, Pune, India, held on 13–14 January 2026. During the conference, he delivered an insightful and forward-looking presentation on “Simulation Safety in Pharmacy Education: Enhancing the Role of the Clinical Pharmacist in the Patient Care Process.” His talk highlighted the critical importance of simulation-based education in preparing pharmacy graduates for safe, effective, and patient-centered clinical practice.

In addition to his keynote participation at the conference, Professor Baig was also invited to speak at several prestigious pharmacy institutions in Pune, including Modern College of Pharmacy, Bharati Vidyapeeth University, and Poona College of Pharmacy. These academic interactions provided an excellent platform for knowledge exchange and academic collaboration between institutions in India and the United Arab Emirates.

During his lectures, Professor Baig showcased how Dubai Medical University stands at the forefront of innovation in health professions education by integrating advanced simulation technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and virtual reality (VR) into its pharmacy curriculum. He emphasized that DMU adopts a learner-centered, competency-based educational model, where students are trained extensively in high-fidelity simulated environments that closely replicate real clinical settings.

This progressive approach ensures that DMU pharmacy students develop strong clinical decision-making, communication, and patient safety skills before being deployed to professional experiential training sites. By allowing students to practice and refine their competencies in a controlled, risk-free environment, DMU significantly enhances patient safety while producing practice-ready clinical pharmacists.

Professor Baig’s presentations strongly reflected DMU’s commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and global best practices in pharmacy education, reinforcing the university’s reputation as a regional and international leader in simulation-based healthcare training.

title: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy and Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society Sign MoU to Advance Clinical Pharmacy in the UAE

This milestone agreement marks a significant step forward in strengthening collaboration between academic institutions and professional societies to advance
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy proudly announces the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society (ECPS) during a formal ceremony held at the Dubai Medical University campus. This milestone agreement marks a significant step forward in strengthening collaboration between academic institutions and professional societies to advance clinical pharmacy education, training, and practice across the United Arab Emirates.

The MoU builds on the momentum generated during the recent visit of the ECPS Board Team to DMU College of Pharmacy, during which both parties engaged in productive discussions around shared goals, national priorities, and long-term collaboration. The formal signing reflects a shared commitment to fostering excellence in pharmacy education, professional development, research, and community engagement.

The Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society, a newly established national professional society under the umbrella of the Emirates Medical Association, aims to empower clinical pharmacists, support continuing professional education, and enhance patient care outcomes through evidence-based initiatives and strategic partnerships. DMU College of Pharmacy shares this vision and recognizes the importance of strong academic–professional linkages in shaping the future of healthcare in the UAE.

Through this MoU, DMU College of Pharmacy and ECPS will collaborate across several key areas, including joint educational and training activities, clinical placement opportunities, collaborative research and publications, student leadership and professional engagement, and the co-organization and endorsement of scientific events and conferences. The agreement also opens avenues for faculty development initiatives and active participation of DMU faculty and students in ECPS committees and national projects.

title: DMU’s Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini Recognized for Contributions to ICU Pharmacy Education
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University would like to announce that Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor at the College of Pharmacy, has received a Certificate of Appreciation from the SAMS (Syrian American Medical Association) Pharmacy Assembly in recognition of his contributions to pharmacy education in critical care. Dr. El Ouweini was honored
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University would like to announce that Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor at the College of Pharmacy, has received a Certificate of Appreciation from the SAMS (Syrian American Medical Association) Pharmacy Assembly in recognition of his contributions to pharmacy education in critical care.

Dr. El Ouweini was honored for delivering a comprehensive series of Intensive Care Unit (ICU) pharmacotherapy lectures, aimed at advancing high-quality, clinically focused pharmacy education. To date, he has delivered seven specialized lectures, covering key topics in critical care pharmacy practice, including acid–base disorders, anticoagulant reversal, fluid stewardship, antimicrobial stewardship, pain–sedation–delirium management, and cardiogenic shock.

These educational activities reflect Dr. El Ouweini’s commitment to translating evidence-based medicine into practical clinical guidance for pharmacists involved in critical care settings. His lectures have been well received by attendees and are made publicly accessible through recorded sessions to further support continuous professional development.

In recognition of his ongoing educational impact, additional ICU pharmacotherapy lectures are planned for 2026, further strengthening collaboration between academic institutions and professional pharmacy organizations.

Links to all Dr. El Ouweini’s lectures can be found on this YouTube channel:

https://www.youtube.com/@SAMSeducationcommittee

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty Participate in the 17th Global Digital Pharma, Clinical Trials & Drug Delivery Conference
excerpt: Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy, participated in the 17th Global Digital Pharma, Clinical Trials & Drug Delivery Conference, held from December 17–19, 2025, at Novotel Al Barsha, Dubai, UAE, with the active contribution of two faculty members as invited speakers: Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab and Dr. Zahraa Khalifa from the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences.
content:
Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy, participated in the 17th Global Digital Pharma, Clinical Trials & Drug Delivery Conference, held from December 17–19, 2025, at Novotel Al Barsha, Dubai, UAE, with the active contribution of two faculty members as invited speakers: Prof. Naglaa Gamil Shehab and Dr. Zahraa Khalifa from the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences.

Prof. Naglaa Gamil delivered a scientific lecture entitled “Integrating Modern Drug Delivery Systems in Phytochemistry and Herbal Medicine: Nanotechnological Strategies to Improve Anticancer Natural Product Bioavailability.” Her presentation focused on advanced formulation strategies using natural products to enhance bioavailability and effectively target cancer cells through modern drug delivery and nanotechnological approaches. The talk attracted strong engagement and interaction from the audience, reflecting the high relevance and scientific impact of the topic.

Dr. Zahraa Khalifa also contributed to the scientific program of the conference through her presentation entitled “Artificial Intelligence Across the Drug Discovery Pipeline: From Molecule to Market.” Her talk highlighted AI applications across the R&D pipeline, starting from target identification through genomic data analysis, moving through virtual screening and formulation design, and extending to its integration into clinical trial outcome prediction and personalized medicine. The session also offered valuable insights into key ethical, regulatory, and technical considerations.

The conference organizers expressed their great appreciation for the valuable contributions of the DMU faculty members. Their participation highlights the importance of continuous faculty engagement in international scientific conferences to enhance academic visibility, research collaboration, and knowledge exchange.

The College of Pharmacy extends its sincere thanks for the continuous support of the Dean of the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, whose encouragement plays a vital role in promoting faculty participation and excellence at international scientific platforms.

title: DMU Faculty won the best poster prize at the British Pharmacological Society’s Pharmacology 2025 Conference in the UK

title: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy Welcomes Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society to Advance Clinical Pharmacy Education and Practice
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy welcomed the Board Team of the Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society (ECPS) to campus on December 8, 2025, for a strategic visit focused on advancing clinical pharmacy education, professional development, and practice across the United Arab Emirates. The Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society, a newly established national professional body
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy welcomed the Board Team of the Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society (ECPS) to campus on December 8, 2025, for a strategic visit focused on advancing clinical pharmacy education, professional development, and practice across the United Arab Emirates.

The Emirates Clinical Pharmacy Society, a newly established national professional body under the Emirates Medical Association, is dedicated to fostering professional exchange, enhancing continuing education, and strengthening the impact of clinical pharmacists on patient care. The Society brings together clinical practitioners, educators, researchers, and students from across the UAE in pursuit of elevating pharmacy practice standards.

Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, DMU College of Pharmacy faculty member serves as the Scientific Committee Chairperson and plays a key leadership role in shaping the Society’s academic and scientific directions.

During the visit, ECPS President Dr. Saeed Hussein and the ECPS Cultural Committee Chairperson, Dr. Ghattas Abudawoud, along with Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, presented the Society’s mission, current initiatives, and potential pathways for collaboration between ECPS and DMU. Their presentation outlined various opportunities for engagement, including joint educational activities, research collaborations, faculty development initiatives, and expanded professional exposure for pharmacy students.

A significant highlight of the event was the discussion surrounding a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between DMU College of Pharmacy and ECPS. The MoU outlines a multi-faceted partnership aimed at strengthening clinical pharmacy training, supporting scholarly output, enhancing student leadership opportunities, and co-organizing national pharmacy events and conferences.

The visit represents an important milestone in aligning DMU College of Pharmacy with national goals for advancing pharmacy education and clinical practice. Strengthening ties with ECPS is expected to further position DMU as a leading contributor to the UAE’s evolving healthcare and pharmacy landscape.

DMU College of Pharmacy looks forward to the upcoming formal signing of the MoU and to an impactful partnership that will enrich the academic environment, empower future clinical pharmacists, and advance patient-centered care across the nation.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty Contributes to LAU Residency Showcase in Lebanon
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy highlights the international academic engagement of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, who was recently invited as a panelist at the Residency Showcase & Career Strategy event organized by the Lebanese American University (LAU) School of Pharmacy. The event,
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy highlights the international academic engagement of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, who was recently invited as a panelist at the Residency Showcase & Career Strategy event organized by the Lebanese American University (LAU) School of Pharmacy.

The event, held at LAU, brought together PharmD students, residents, alumni, and faculty to discuss the evolving landscape of pharmacy residency training and its impact on career development. Dr. El Ouweini participated in the Alumni Panel, moderated by Dr. Mira El Masri, where he shared insights from his professional journey and highlighted the importance of advanced pharmacy training.

Drawing on his diverse experience across Lebanon and the UAE, Dr. El Ouweini reflected on his path from BPharm training in Syria, to completing his PharmD at LAU, a PGY-1 residency, and later a post-doctoral fellowship in clinical pharmacy research. Today, as a faculty member at DMU, he continues to advance clinical pharmacy education while establishing and expanding critical care services at DMU Hospital.

During the panel discussion, he emphasized how residency training shaped his clinical reasoning, teaching approach, and research capabilities. He also explained how Lebanon’s PGY-1 programs—designed in alignment with U.S. residency standards—equipped him with the competencies needed to practice confidently in international healthcare environments.

He noted that while the field has evolved from BPharm → PharmD → PGY-1, residency remains a “true investment” that enhances a pharmacist’s readiness for both local and global practice.

He encouraged students to embrace opportunities with clarity and ambition, reminding them that residency training builds not only clinical expertise but also leadership, communication, resilience, and teamwork.

On November 16–17, 2025, at the 1st Emirates Pharmacy Society Conference: “Advancing Pharmacy, Leading Tomorrow,” held in Dubai, UAE, fifth-year students from the College of Pharmacy — Dania Abaji, Tasneem Zarzour, Rim Jabr, and Enana Al-Fakih — under the supervision of Dr. Rana Sammour, achieved Second Place in the student research competition.

Their project, titled “MediCycle: AI-Driven Solutions for Sustainable Pharmaceutical Waste Management,” was recognized for its innovative use of AI technology and smart systems to promote environmental sustainability and responsible medication disposal.

The initiative was commended for its potential real-world application, with possible collaborations under discussion with Beeah and other sustainability partners.

In addition, two other students from the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, Ms. Marwa Hadi and Ms. Jumana Al-Ansari, showcased their innovative research project titled “PharmaTwinX: The Novel Dual Digital Twin AI Model for Precision Medicine Pharmacotherapy” at the First Emirates Pharmacy Society Conference. The project was presented under the supervision of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University.

PharmaTwinX introduces a pioneering dual digital-twin AI model that virtually pairs a “Patient Twin” and a “Drug Twin” to simulate and predict individualized drug responses prior to therapy initiation.

The research objective is to develop a proof-of-concept AI platform capable of predicting individualized drug efficacy, safety, and formulation stability by virtually pairing drug and patient models prior to therapy initiation. This innovative approach aims to reduce adverse drug reactions and optimize personalized therapy outcomes through AI-driven simulation and predictive modeling.

Looking ahead, the research team plans to advance the model’s capabilities by integrating wearable sensors, paediatric and geriatric modules, and reinforcement-learning-based dose optimization. These future directions aim to enhance real-world applicability and pave the way for AI-assisted, pharmacist-led precision pharmacotherapy.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Hosts Faculty Development Seminar on Building a Collaborative-Ready Healthcare Workforce
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy hosted a cross-college Faculty Development Seminar delivered by Dr. Eman Moussa El-Labbad, Associate Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at the College of Pharmacy, Ain Shams University, Egypt. Dr. El-Labbad is also a Board Member of the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration (ANIC) and Co-Facilitator with Interprofessional.Global, bringing extensive
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy hosted a cross-college Faculty Development Seminar delivered by Dr. Eman Moussa El-Labbad, Associate Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at the College of Pharmacy, Ain Shams University, Egypt. Dr. El-Labbad is also a Board Member of the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration (ANIC) and Co-Facilitator with Interprofessional.Global, bringing extensive expertise in interprofessional education and collaborative practice (IPE/IPC) across the Arab region

The seminar, titled “Towards a Collaborative-Ready Healthcare Workforce: Designing a Longitudinal IPE/IPC Curriculum,” was attended by faculty members from all three DMU colleges — Pharmacy, Medicine, and Nursing.
Dr. El-Labbad emphasized the growing need for “collaborative-ready” healthcare professionals who can deliver safe, person-centered care through teamwork and effective communication. She highlighted the World Health Organization’s IPE framework and shared global best practices for embedding interprofessional learning in health education.

During the interactive session, participants explored how future healthcare providers can be equipped to work together across disciplines to improve patient outcomes. Dr. El-Labbad discussed models of interprofessional learning grounded in experiential, situated, and community-of-practice theories, and demonstrated how faculty roles must evolve from traditional lecturers to facilitators of collaborative learning.

Following the seminar, Dr. El-Labbad conducted a focused workshop with the DMU Interprofessional Education (IPE) Committee titled “Co-Designing a Longitudinal IPE/IPC Curriculum Blueprint: A Structured Approach Using Tyler’s Model.” This practical session guided committee members through a series of structured group tasks to design a university-wide IPE framework

By the end of the workshop, the DMU IPE Committee had drafted a clear roadmap for integrating interprofessional education across the longitudinal curriculum, fostering collaboration, and ensuring that all DMU graduates are prepared to work effectively in interprofessional healthcare teams.

title: Panelist in SimTalks: the Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Healthcare Simulation
excerpt: As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally,
content:
As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally, alongside educators, healthcare professionals, and students, to explore the evolving role of technology in clinical education.

Dr. Sanad emphasized the importance of balancing technological innovation with human-centered care, noting that empathy, intuition, and professional judgment remain essential in training future clinicians. She highlighted the need for equitable access, demonstrating that meaningful learning can be achieved through low-fidelity models, creative approaches, and collaborative partnerships, even in the absence of high-cost VR/AR/AI equipment.

Looking ahead to 2035, Dr. Sanad predicted that students will increasingly engage with AI-driven virtual environments, but she stressed that these tools must complement, not replace, real-world bedside experiences. She offered actionable recommendations for educators, including aligning technology with learning outcomes, empowering faculty to adapt tools, promoting creativity and equity, and keeping patient safety, resilience, and humanity at the core of simulation-based education.

The session highlighted both the promise and limitations of immersive technologies, reaffirming the value of blended learning models that combine virtual simulation with bedside practice to prepare competent, empathetic, and resilient healthcare professionals.

content:
The College of Nursing at Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly participated in the SANID Program, a national volunteer initiative dedicated to training individuals to effectively respond to disasters and emergencies across the UAE.

Held from June 2nd to 4th, 2025 at the DMU Building (Second Floor, Rooms 207 & 208), the program brought together nursing students and faculty members for three days of intensive training that combined lecture-based instruction with hands-on practical sessions.

The training covered a wide range of essential emergency preparedness and response skills, including:

  1. Preparing for disasters
  2. Leadership in crisis situations
  3. Fire safety and prevention
  4. Psychological reactions to disasters
  5. Search and rescue operations
  6. Injury triage and classification
  7. Raising awareness about terrorism
  8. Lifting and securing techniques
