title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Concludes WinTernship 2026 in Integrative Medicine
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) successfully conducted the Winter Internship “WinTernship 2026”, a one-week intensive program held from 5–9 January, under the supervision of Dr. Naglaa Saad, Head of the Integrative Medicine Department and Assistant Dean – Quality & Accreditation. The internship brought together students from the Colleges of Pharmacy, Medicine,
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) successfully conducted the Winter Internship “WinTernship 2026”, a one-week intensive program held from 5–9 January, under the supervision of Dr. Naglaa Saad, Head of the Integrative Medicine Department and Assistant Dean – Quality & Accreditation.

The internship brought together students from the Colleges of Pharmacy, Medicine, and Nursing, underscoring DMU’s commitment to interprofessional education (IPE) and collaborative healthcare training. The program provided focused, evidence-based exposure to integrative and complementary medicine.

Throughout the week, students engaged in interactive workshops and hands-on sessions covering herbal medicine, acupuncture, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), and cupping therapy, with particular emphasis on evidence-based herbal medicine and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in herbal formulation design and optimization.

A key component of WinTernship 2026 was the interprofessional group project, in which mixed student teams identified healthcare needs and developed AI-informed, evidence-based herbal product concepts, fostering collaboration, clinical reasoning, innovation, and communication skills.

Through WinTernship 2026, Dubai Medical University continues to demonstrate leadership in integrative medicine education. Such multidisciplinary internships integrating traditional medicine, modern science, AI, and interprofessional learning remain unique to DMU, both regionally and nationally.

title: College of Pharmacy has successfully concluded the Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA) Training Series
excerpt: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy has successfully concluded the Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA) Training Series for its Pharmacy Practice faculty members. Conducted from February to April 2025, the series forms part of the College’s ongoing professional development initiatives aimed at enhancing the proficiency in clinical pharmacy education and assessment. This training series was
content:
Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy has successfully concluded the Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA) Training Series for its Pharmacy Practice faculty members.

Conducted from February to April 2025, the series forms part of the College’s ongoing professional development initiatives aimed at enhancing the proficiency in clinical pharmacy education and assessment.
This training series was launched as part of embedding the PSA into the pharmacy curriculum, with the goal of strengthening student competencies in safe and effective prescribing practices.

Faculty members engaged in a series of interactive, case-based, and hands-on sessions covering the eight core domains of the PSA:
1. Prescribing
2. Prescription Review
3. Planning Management
4. Providing Information
5. Calculation Skills
6. Adverse Drug Reactions
7. Drug Monitoring
8. Data Interpretation

These domains represent critical competencies aligned with the international Prescribing Safety Assessment framework and are vital for preparing pharmacy students for real-world clinical practice.

The College extends its sincere appreciation to all faculty members for their active participation and valuable contributions to the success of this initiative. Special thanks to Dr. Rizah Anwar Assadi, PharmD, BCPS , who led and facilitated the implementation of PSA at DMU and played a key role in supporting its integration into the academic framework.

title: Pharmacy Beyond The Planet: Dubai Medical University & University of Nottingham Dive into Medications in Space
excerpt: On Wednesday, April 23, 2025, the IVPN Student Club at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an inspiring international webinar in collaboration with the University of Nottingham, titled "Astropharmacy: The Science and Practice of Medication in Spaceflight." The event featured two speakers — Phil Williams Associate Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Li Shean Toh , Assistant Professor — who
content:
On Wednesday, April 23, 2025, the IVPN Student Club at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an inspiring international webinar in collaboration with the University of Nottingham, titled "Astropharmacy: The Science and Practice of Medication in Spaceflight." The event featured two speakers — Phil Williams Associate Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Li Shean Toh , Assistant Professor — who shared fascinating insights into the unique challenges of providing pharmaceutical care during space missions.

The webinar sparked lively interest among pharmacy students from various universities, who tuned in to learn about how medications behave in zero gravity, how astronauts receive care during long-term missions, and the future role of pharmacists in space exploration. Beyond the science, the session encouraged students to think creatively and globally about their profession.

Bringing together academic expertise and student curiosity, this event is a testament to DMU’s dedication to delivering forward-thinking pharmacy education and building meaningful international partnerships that enrich the student learning experience.

Building on the success of the event, DMU students are now collaborating with Dr. Phil Williams and his team at the University of Nottingham to initiate a new research project focused on advancing the field of astropharmacy. This exciting development reflects DMU’s dedication to nurturing research opportunities, global collaboration, and innovation in pharmacy education.

title: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy Hosts Inspiring Workshop by Dr. Osama Tabbara
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University recently welcomed Dr. Osama Tabbara, President of the IVPN-Network, for an engaging and motivational workshop titled “The Skills & Qualities of Impressive Pharmacists: Raise your Self Awareness.” The session, attended by both faculty members and pharmacy students, focused on the evolving landscape of pharmacy practice and the
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University recently welcomed Dr. Osama Tabbara, President of the IVPN-Network, for an engaging and motivational workshop titled “The Skills & Qualities of Impressive Pharmacists: Raise your Self Awareness.”

The session, attended by both faculty members and pharmacy students, focused on the evolving landscape of pharmacy practice and the critical role of transformational leadership, adaptability, and professionalism in driving the profession forward.

Drawing on his extensive experience as a consultant and pharmacy leader, Dr. Tabbara inspired participants to embrace a mindset of continuous improvement and innovation. He highlighted the challenges facing the modern pharmacist — from increased competition and complex clinical responsibilities to the need for agility in a rapidly changing healthcare environment.

Through his “12 Impressive Habits” framework, Dr. Tabbara guided attendees on key personal and professional traits essential for career growth. These habits included punctuality, communication skills, visibility, engagement, adaptability, emotional intelligence, and time management, among others. Each habit was accompanied by practical self-assessment tools, encouraging participants to reflect on their own professional development.

Dr. Tabbara also emphasized the importance of mentorship, self-awareness, and teamwork, urging students to “become brands of excellence” within the pharmacy profession. His closing message, “Don’t ask when I can be promoted — ask how I can be great and impressive,” resonated strongly with the audience.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Shines at the 12th GCC Pharmacy Congress
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University participated in the 12th GCC Pharmacy Congress, held on October 31– November 2, 2025, at Dubai, UAE. The event brought together international experts and pharmacy leaders to discuss cutting-edge advancements in pharmacotherapy, Pharmacoeconomics, pharmacogenomics, value-based care, leadership, entrepreneurship, digital health, and patient-centered practices. The College of Pharmacy
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University participated in the 12th GCC Pharmacy Congress, held on October 31– November 2, 2025, at Dubai, UAE. The event brought together international experts and pharmacy leaders to discuss cutting-edge advancements in pharmacotherapy, Pharmacoeconomics, pharmacogenomics, value-based care, leadership, entrepreneurship, digital health, and patient-centered practices.

The College of Pharmacy had a strong presence at the conference, with faculty and pharmacy students attending sessions on antimicrobial stewardship, transplant pharmacotherapy, pediatrics, oncology, and digital health innovations. Their active participation provided an invaluable opportunity to engage with global leaders in clinical pharmacy and gain insights into the latest research and best practices.

Additionally, Dr. Sahar Elnajjar. Clinical Lecturer and Preceptor at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University, presented her research titled “Impact of Post-Prescription Review on Therapeutic Appropriateness in Community-Acquired Pneumonia” at the *12th GCC Pharmacy Congress 2025*, highlighting the effectiveness of clinical pharmacist-led antimicrobial stewardship in a UAE hospitals.

Additionally, Dubai Medical University students presented two innovative research posters developed under the supervision of Dr. Naglaa Saad as part of their Herbal and Integrative Medicine summer internship program.

The first project, GastroHeal – An AI-Powered Herbal Solution for Synergistic Management of Helicobacter pylori, introduced an AI-guided herbal effervescent formulation combining licorice, turmeric, ginger, chamomile, and hibiscus to combat H. pylori infection while soothing and protecting the stomach lining.

The second project, Scentella™ – AI-Driven Prototype Regrowth Control Gel, showcased a natural, non-hormonal formulation enriched with aloe vera, niacinamide, and botanical extracts such as Cyperus and turmeric. Designed to gently reduce unwanted facial hair growth, it offers a safe, moisturizing, and sustainable skincare solution for women.
By combining academic excellence with practical training, the College continues to empower its students and faculty to contribute meaningfully to improving patient care and healthcare systems across the region.

title: DMU’s Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini Represents University at European Society of Intensive Care Medicine LIVES 2025 in Munich
excerpt: Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), proudly represented the university at the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) LIVES 2025 Congress held in Munich between October 25-29, 2025. As the Lead of Social Media and Digital
content:
Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), proudly represented the university at the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) LIVES 2025 Congress held in Munich between October 25-29, 2025.

As the Lead of Social Media and Digital Branding for the Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapy Section of ESICM, Dr. El Ouweini played an active role in shaping the scientific and professional discourse of this prestigious international meeting.

During the congress, Dr. El Ouweini moderated two high-level debate sessions in the Pharmacotherapy Lounge.

The first session centered on the BLING III Trial, exploring how the adoption of continuous beta-lactam infusion in intensive care units (ICUs) requires balancing potential clinical benefits with practical challenges such as infusion pump availability, pharmacy preparation logistics, staff training, and workflow adjustments.
The discussion also highlighted the evolving role of ICU pharmacist prescribers in addressing workforce shortages, streamlining care, and leveraging pharmacotherapy expertise to enhance patient safety and operational efficiency through therapeutic drug monitoring and electronic prescribing systems.

In his capacity as part of the ESICM Social Media & Communication Team, Dr. El Ouweini collaborated with an international group of clinicians and scientists to bring the congress’s science, discussions, and innovations to the global critical care community. The team engaged actively in key scientific sessions, sharing insights and promoting conversations on how new research findings can translate into real-world clinical practice.

Additionally, Dr. El Ouweini moderated the Pharmacotherapy and Pharmacology Section poster abstract session, an engaging forum featuring eight critical care clinicians from Europe and Asia who presented their latest research on essential pharmacotherapy topics.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Faculty Bridging Green Innovation and Collaborative Learning in Pharmacy Education

Dubai Medical University Pharmacy Students showcased innovation, teamwork, and sustainability in an engaging “Sustainable Cosmeceuticals Workshop” conducted by Prof. Bazigha K. The workshop strengthened key competencies in sustainability, collaboration, and innovation, reflecting the College’s educational mission. The active learning session, held in the inspiring DMU Greenhouse, offered a hands-on learning experience that linked scientific knowledge with creativity and environmental responsibility. Students explored the greenhouse to identify their “Hero Herb”, studied its therapeutic properties, and proposed suitable dosage forms, eco-friendly packaging, and labeling concepts for sustainable cosmetic products.

To extend learning beyond observation, students participated in Team-Based Learning (TBL) activities, where they worked collaboratively in groups and were evaluated through Individual Readiness Assurance Tests (iRATs) and Group Readiness Assurance Tests (gRATs). Using Mentimeter software, participants actively engaged in real-time quizzes and discussions, thereby enhancing interaction, communication, and critical thinking.

The workshop reflected the students’ enthusiasm and leadership in shaping a greener, more innovative, and more sustainable future for pharmacy practice.

The Dubai Medical University (DMU) Simulation Center proudly celebrated International Simulation Week during the week of 15 to 17 September 2025, a global initiative recognized by the Society for Simulation in Healthcare (SSH). Students not only showcased their clinical and technical skills but also discovered the importance of communication, leadership, and adaptability in healthcare practice.

The African Phytomedicine Scientific Society (APSS) is a scientific community that aims to stimulate and facilitate the interaction of
content:
Dubai Medical University is pleased to announce that Dr. Naglaa Saad, Associate Professor and Assistant Dean- Quality & Accreditation College of Pharmacy, has been appointed as a Board Member of the African Phytomedicine Scientific Society (APSS).
The African Phytomedicine Scientific Society (APSS) is a scientific community that aims to stimulate and facilitate the interaction of African researchers in the field of medicinal plant science. Its mission is to foster the scientific development of the continent in ethnopharmacology and natural products research, while also promoting collaboration, resource sharing, and professional exchange among its members. The society provides a dynamic platform for sharing relevant scientific opportunities, announcing international events, and advancing partnerships in laboratory research and technology acquisition.
APSS held its 1st Annual International Congress under the theme “Inspired by Mother Nature: Pharmaceuticals and Cosmeceuticals” on 9–10 November 2023 at the University of Pretoria, South Africa. Dr. Saad was honored with theBest Oral Presentation Awardat this congress.
Most recently, APSS had its second congress jointly with the 23rd International Congress of the International Society for Ethnopharmacology (ISE), held from 23–26 October 2024 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa. Dr. Saad served as a member of the Scientific Committee and delivered an oral presentation, showcasing her recent research in the field of drug discovery from natural products.
Dr. Saad’s appointment to the APSS Board is a vital step in her contributions to natural products research and integrative medicine. Her role will strengthen collaboration between the UAE and African and international scientific communities, advancing shared goals in herbal medicine, ethnopharmacology, and innovative therapeutic discovery.
Dubai Medical University extends its congratulations to Dr. Naglaa Saad on this recognition and looks forward to her continued impact on global phytomedicine research.

title: College of Pharmacy Faculty and Students Publish Review Article in International Peer-Reviewed Journal
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a review article by faculty members and undergraduate pharmacy students in Biomaterials Translational, an internationally recognized peer-reviewed journal at the forefront of translational medicine and biomaterials science. The article, titled “Cubosomes as smart nanocarriers for antimicrobial agents: A review of emerging applications,”
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) announces the publication of a review article by faculty members and undergraduate pharmacy students in Biomaterials Translational, an internationally recognized peer-reviewed journal at the forefront of translational medicine and biomaterials science.

The article, titled “Cubosomes as smart nanocarriers for antimicrobial agents: A review of emerging applications,” was authored by Prof. Bazigha K. Abdul Rasool and Prof. Aliasgar Shahiwala from the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, alongside undergraduate pharmacy students Raneem Zakaria and Nour Hijazi.

The review explores cubosomes — an innovative class of lipid-based nanoparticles — and their promising role in delivering antimicrobial agents. Unlike conventional drug carriers, cubosomes possess a highly ordered internal structure that allows them to efficiently encapsulate a wide range of drug types while providing sustained and controlled release. The article highlights the potential of these advanced nanocarriers to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal drugs, and to overcome major challenges such as antimicrobial resistance, rapid drug degradation, and poor drug permeability. The review also discusses their ability to disrupt biofilms and improve targeted drug delivery, alongside current limitations in large-scale manufacturing and storage stability that must be addressed before clinical translation.

The article is available open access at:

https://doi.org/10.12336/bmt.25.00050

Following the presentation, participants engaged in the Protect & Detect Demonstration, an activity designed in a case study format to encourage practical learning. This session provided hands-on experience and interactive discussions on breast self-examination and the importance of early detection in saving lives.

Adding an element of fun and friendly competition, attendees participated in the Spin the Wheel (Fact or Myth) game — a quiz-based activity that tested participants’ knowledge about breast cancer, debunking common myths and reinforcing accurate information about prevention and care. The day concluded with the Cup Stack Challenge, where teams worked together to build the tallest pink cup tower, symbolizing unity, awareness, and collective action against breast cancer.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Shines at the 5th SEHA International Clinical Pharmacy Conference

content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University proudly participated in the 5th SEHA International Clinical Pharmacy Conference (SICPC 2025), held on September 26–27, 2025, at the Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers. The event brought together international experts and clinical pharmacy leaders to discuss cutting-edge advancements in pharmacotherapy, critical care, and patient-centered practices.

Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor in the Department of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, represented the College as an invited speaker. He delivered an engaging presentation titled “Optimizing Sedation Strategies in the ICU: Pharmacist-Driven Protocols”, during the Advances in Pharmacotherapy–Critical Care session. In his talk, Dr. El Ouweini highlighted the importance of evidence-based sedation practices, the clinical advantages of non-benzodiazepine agents, and the role of pharmacist-led sedation protocols in improving patient outcomes. He emphasized how clinical pharmacists can champion ICU liberation strategies, reduce delirium, and enhance recovery through multidisciplinary collaboration.

The College of Pharmacy had a strong presence at the conference, with faculty and pharmacy students attending sessions on antimicrobial stewardship, transplant pharmacotherapy, pediatrics, oncology, and digital health innovations. Their active participation provided an invaluable opportunity to engage with global leaders in clinical pharmacy and gain insights into the latest research and best practices.

By combining academic excellence with practical training, the College continues to empower its students and faculty to contribute meaningfully to improving patient care and healthcare systems across the region.

title: Dubai Medical University Concludes UAE’s First Internship in Herbal and Integrative Medicine
excerpt: Dubai Medical University successfully concluded the first internship of its kind in the UAE and the region, a four-week program titled "Herbal and Integrative Medicine Internship". The internship was led by Dr. Naglaa Saad, Associate Professor at the College of Pharmacy. Designed to merge traditional healing systems with modern science, the internship offered students an
content:
Dubai Medical University successfully concluded the first internship of its kind in the UAE and the region, a four-week program titled "Herbal and Integrative Medicine Internship". The internship was led by Dr. Naglaa Saad, Associate Professor at the College of Pharmacy.
Designed to merge traditional healing systems with modern science, the internship offered students an immersive experience across four major themes:

  • AI-Powered Complementary Medicine
  • Herbal Medicine: From Lab to Market
  • Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)
  • Foundations of Homeopathy

The program featured distinguished guest speakers who enriched the learning experience. Dr. Li Haufei, a Chinese UAE-licensed acupuncturist, introduced students to the history and principles of Traditional Chinese Medicine and acupuncture in the UAE. Dr. Mariam Al-Tharaawi, a UAE-licensed pharmacist and Hijama practitioner, offered in-depth sessions on the practice and therapeutic value of Hijama. Additionally, Dr. Shivani Sharma, a UAE-licensed homeopathy practitioner, provided students with valuable insights into the foundational principles and clinical applications of homeopathy.
A key highlight of the internship was the hands-on, project-based learning model. Students formed six interprofessional teams, composed of pharmacy and medicine students, and collaboratively developed AI-driven herbal product prototypesin DMU’s laboratories with the guidance of Dr. Yasmen Yasser. The students’ products targeted common health conditions such as H. pylori infection, constipation, diarrhea, eczema, hirsutism, and polycystic ovarian syndrome.

The program concluded with a Grande Finale presentation day, where each team pitched their product prototypes to a distinguished panel comprising Prof. Sherief Khalifa (Vice Chancellor, Academic Affairs & Dean, College of Pharmacy), Engineer Hessa Lootah(Dubai Medical University AI & Innovation Lead) and Dr. Naglaa Saad(Internship Leader), and who all provided expert feedback on clinical value, formulation, and market readiness.
Six awards were presented to recognize outstanding achievements:

  • Best Innovation Award
  • Best Formulation Award
  • Best Branding Award
  • Best Clinical Relevance Award
  • Most Market-Ready Product Award
  • Best Use of Local Herbs Award

Prof. Sherief Khalifa remarked, “This initiative reflects our commitment to innovation in healthcare education. The students demonstrated an impressive blend of creativity, teamwork, and evidence-based thinking.”
This internship has set a new benchmark for integrative medicine education in the UAE and beyond, paving the way for future interdisciplinary collaborations and innovation-driven learning.

title: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy presents at the Fifth Women in Research Forum (QUWA)

content:
We are delighted to share that two research projects from the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University were shortlisted at the Fifth Women in Research Forum (QUWA) organized by the University of Sharjah, standing out among 900 poster submissions evaluated by 300 distinguished reviewers!
Dr. Hanan Anbar and Dr. Yosra Lozon presented their research project alongside their undergraduate students,Rahma Nasir, Maryam Al Nazir, Rim Jabr, and Tasneem Zarzour from the College of Pharmacy, as well as Sana Ahmed and Rokia Malahifci from the College of Medicine. Their project was the result of a collaborative effort between Dubai Medical University, working with colleagues from the University of Sharjah, Gulf Medical University, and the University of Oxford.

Additionally, Dr. Semira Beshir presented her research project in collaboration with colleagues from the Fatima College in Abu Dhabi.

The Women in Research Forum, hosted by the University of Sharjah, is a distinguished platform dedicated to recognizing and advancing the achievements of women researchers across diverse fields and highlight the importance of the interdisciplinary work, and international research collaborations in advancing knowledge and inspiring the next generation of scientists.

content:
We would like to announce that Prof. Mirza R. His talk emphasized the importance of evidence-based approaches, interdisciplinary collaboration, and innovative therapeutic strategies to enhance patient care.

The event featured renowned specialists from the USA, India, and the UAE, facilitating discussions on cutting-edge research and groundbreaking clinical strategies.
The future of pain management is interdisciplinary, uniting knowledge, expertise, and innovation to improve patient outcomes.

title: Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy Enhances Academic Advising for Student Success
excerpt: At Dubai Medical University, we are dedicated to continuous faculty development and advancing academic advising practices to support our students’ learning journeys and future careers. Recently, Dr. Doaa Kamal AlKhalidi, Assistant Professor in the Pharmacy Practice Department, attended a transformative workshop organized by CLICKS on “Enhancing Student Success Through Developing a Robust Academic Advising System.”
content:
At Dubai Medical University, we are dedicated to continuous faculty development and advancing academic advising practices to support our students’ learning journeys and future careers.

Recently, Dr. Doaa Kamal AlKhalidi, Assistant Professor in the Pharmacy Practice Department, attended a transformative workshop organized by CLICKS on “Enhancing Student Success Through Developing a Robust Academic Advising System.”

Led by Dr. Narimane Hadj Hamou, the session was highly interactive and brought together educators from across the region to exchange best practices and strategies for strengthening academic advising. The workshop highlighted that academic advising is not merely a support service but a vital component of the student learning experience—helping both struggling and high-achieving students navigate their academic paths effectively.

  • Key topics covered included:
  • – Learning-centered academic advising systems
  • – Different approaches and types of student support
  • – Best practices for student engagement
  • – Strategies to overcome challenges in academic advising

A special thanks to CLICKS and Dr. Narimane Hadj Hamou for this valuable learning experience. We look forward to implementing new strategies to enhance student success at Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy.

Dubai Medical University’s College of Pharmacy came alive with enthusiasm on February 12, 2025, as students and faculty gathered for “Pharmacy Around the Globe”, an interactive event showcasing global pharmacy practices. Organized in collaboration with DPCSU-IPSF, DPC-IVPN, and the Community Engagement Team, the event provided an enriching platform to explore advancements in pharmacy across diverse regions of the world.

The event featured six interactive stations, each representing one of the World Health Organization (WHO) regions: Africa, the Americas, South-East Asia, Europe, the Eastern Mediterranean, and the Western Pacific. This initiative not only celebrated the diverse scope of pharmacy worldwide but also reinforced the shared vision of pharmacists in delivering quality healthcare across borders.

title: Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025
excerpt: We are thrilled to announce that fourth-year B.Pharm students Rahma Nasir, Maryam Elnazier, Naiba Khusrau, Jannat Akram, and Haneen Badreldin from Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025! Their innovative project, titled “Enhancing Healthcare Outcomes through an Advanced Pill Reminder App: A Novel Approach
content:
We are thrilled to announce that fourth-year B.Pharm students Rahma Nasir, Maryam Elnazier, Naiba Khusrau, Jannat Akram, and Haneen Badreldin from Dubai Medical University have been awarded the Gold Award at the International Creative Innovation Idea Competition (ICIIC) 2025!

Their innovative project, titled “Enhancing Healthcare Outcomes through an Advanced Pill Reminder App: A Novel Approach to Improving Medication Adherence and Compliance,” has garnered international recognition under the expert guidance of Prof. Aliasgar Shahiwala.

This groundbreaking app addresses a crucial challenge in medication adherence. By offering timely reminders, medication tracking, and an intuitive user interface, the app empowers patients to take their medications as prescribed, ultimately improving health outcomes.

In addition to winning the Gold Award, the team also secured an RM100 cash prize in the ‘YouTube Lucky Draw’ contest! Check out their presentation video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gerp1G185fc

The ICIIC is a prestigious platform that evaluates innovative ideas based on novelty, impact, and feasibility, and we couldn’t be prouder of our students for excelling on this global stage.

title: Monash University Delegation Visits Dubai Medical College for Girls (Dubai Medical University) to Strengthen Academic Collaboration
excerpt: Dubai, January 2025 – A delegation from Monash University, led by Professor Craig Jeffrey, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (International) and Senior Vice-President, and Dr. Nizar Farjou, Associate President – Middle East, North Africa & Central Asia – Global Engagement, visited Dubai Medical College for Girls (DMCG) as part of their strategic engagement with key institutions in the UAE.During their visit, the delegation met
content:
Dubai, January 2025 – A delegation from Monash University, led by Professor Craig Jeffrey, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (International) and Senior Vice-President, and Dr. Nizar Farjou, Associate President – Middle East, North Africa & Central Asia – Global Engagement, visited Dubai Medical College for Girls (DMCG) as part of their strategic engagement with key institutions in the UAE.
During their visit, the delegation met with the Dean Prof. Yousif Eltayeb, Acting Associate Dean of Research Dr. Shifan Khanday, Prof. AbdelMoniem Elmardi Acting associate dean of academic affairs and Eng Hessa Lootah AI and Innovation lead at Saeed Ahmad Lootah Charity Foundation (SALCF) to discuss potential avenues for academic collaboration under Monash University’s Anchoring Strategy. This initiative aims to identify Anchor Collaborators and Anchor Missions, prioritizing international partnerships through long-term capacity building and trust.

The meeting focused on key areas such as:

  • Joint research initiatives in medical education, AI in healthcare, and precision medicine.
  • Student and faculty exchange programs to promote knowledge sharing.
  • Integration of AI in medical education through Monash and DMCG’s shared expertise.
  • Opportunities for collaborative degree programs and training workshops.

Speaking about the visit, Dr. Nizar Farjou stated:
“Our discussions with DMCG reflect Monash University’s commitment to strengthening international partnerships. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and look forward to building a sustainable and impactful collaboration.”
The visit marks a significant step toward deepening academic ties between Monash University and leading institutions in the UAE, reinforcing both parties’ commitment to advancing healthcare education and research. Further steps and formal agreements are expected to follow as the partnership develops.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Marks the Successful Conclusion of the Preceptor Certificate Program in Collaboration with AACP and ACPE
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University is pleased to share that the fourth and final session of the Preceptor Certificate Program took place on January 12th, 2025. The full-day in-person session, titled “Taking Precepting to Another Level Through Case-Based Application,” provided participants with the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they had
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University is pleased to share that the fourth and final session of the Preceptor Certificate Program took place on January 12th, 2025.

The full-day in-person session, titled “Taking Precepting to Another Level Through Case-Based Application,” provided participants with the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they had gained during the previous preparatory sessions. Throughout the day, 28 preceptors from 11 institutions worked collaboratively in small groups, tackling complex case scenarios that addressed real-world preceptor-learner challenges.

We were honored to have Dr. Craig D. Cox from Texas Tech University and Dr. Bassam Atallah from Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi as our speakers and facilitators for this session.

This program spanned four sessions in total. The journey began in September 2024 with the first session, “Start of Preceptor Journey – Self Discovery,” delivered by:

  • Dr. Craig D. Cox (Professor, Regional Dean, and Division Head – Medicine, Texas Tech University HSC Jerry H Hodge School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Kate Newman (Associate Professor & Director of Experiential Education, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Bassam Atallah (Clinical Associate Professor, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine).

The second session, held in October 2024, was titled “Start of Rotation – Learner/Site Preparation” and was delivered by:

  • Dr. Suzanne Larson (Director, Experiential Education, Midwestern University College of Pharmacy, Glendale, AZ Campus)
  • Dr. Megan Kaun (Director of Experiential Education, The University of Toledo, College of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences)
  • Dr. Nicole Gebran Connell, PharmD, BCPS, SQIL(HMS) (Senior Specialist Pharmacist – Clinical Pharmacy Lead, Dubai Health).

The third session, held in November 2024, focused on “The Feedback Experience: One Step at a Time” and was delievered by:

  • Dr. Angela Brownfield (Director of Experiential Learning & IPPE Coordinator, Clinical Professor, University of Missouri Kansas City (UMKC) School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Rucha Bond (Clinical Professor, Pharmacy Practice Division, Assistant Dean for Experiential Education, The University of Texas at Austin, College of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Sahar Elnajjar (Lecturer and Clinical Preceptor, College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University).

At the conclusion of the final session, preceptors were awarded Certificates of Program Completion, recognizing their dedication to enhancing their preceptorship skills.

We would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to all the instructors who contributed to delivering this program and to the the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) and to the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) for their collaboration and support.

This program’s success serves as the foundation for many more initiatives to come. We are excited to continue offering similar programs in the future, further developing our preceptors and contributing to the growth of pharmacy education and practice, both in the UAE and beyond!

Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with ACPE and AACP, Co-Organizes the Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) proudly co-organized the 8th Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop on January 10-11, 2025.

The workshop brought together pharmacy education leaders from 24 colleges across the region, representing countries such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Libya, Iraq, Lebanon, Jordan, and all pharmacy colleges in the UAE.

The event welcomed approximately 12 deans of pharmacy colleges and esteemed faculty members, creating a vibrant platform for knowledge exchange, networking, and enhancing best practices in pharmacy education.

Key topics addressed during the workshop included:

– Best Practices in Experiential Education and Preceptor Development.
– Competency-Based Assessment, Grading and Skills Assessment.
-Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education and Use by Academic Staff.

This two-day event provided an exceptional opportunity to strengthen collaboration among pharmacy colleges across the region, fostering innovation and excellence in teaching and learning.

As co-organizers, the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University expresses its sincere appreciation to all participants, including deans, faculty members, and representatives, for their active involvement and invaluable contributions, which made the workshop a success.

content:
On Monday January 6, 2025, a delegation from the American Pharmacists Association (APhA): Daniel Zlott Senior Vice President, Education & Business Development and Michael Rouse Senior Director, Global Initiatives entered signed an agreement with Dubai Pharmacy College (DPC). The agreement aims to advance the scope of practice of Pharmacy in the UAE to include immunization. APhA will train faculty, licensed pharmacists and students of DPC to become certified immunizers by APhA. The immunization training course will become part of the study plan for the Pharmacy degree program at DPC.

Dean Khalifa commented: “We are excited about our partnership with APhA and we are hoping that our initiatives with APhA will be contagious to all colleges of pharmacy in the UAE and the region. We believe that it is time to make use of the pharmacists’ workforce that has been underutilized for decades.”

title: Regulating Adaptive Competency-Based Learning through Workplace-Based Assessment: DMCG’s Journey
excerpt: As the paradigm in medical education shifts from traditional to programmatic assessment models, the emphasis has moved toward providing authentic assessments—those that immerse students in real-life clinical experiences. Such assessments are crucial for delivering ongoing, meaningful feedback on student competence and performance, a cornerstone of the educational process. As a result, Workplace-based assessment is now
content:
As the paradigm in medical education shifts from traditional to programmatic assessment models, the emphasis has moved toward providing authentic assessments—those that immerse students in real-life clinical experiences. Such assessments are crucial for delivering ongoing, meaningful feedback on student competence and performance, a cornerstone of the educational process. As a result, Workplace-based assessment is now considered an essential method for continuous and comprehensive student evaluation during clinical training. Dr. Heba Ismail, a Teaching Assistant at Dubai Medical College for Girls, presented DMCG’s experience in implementing workplace-based assessment using Blue at the Bluenotes MENA 2024 Conference hosted by Zayed University. The presentation addressed the expectations met, challenges encountered, and the next steps.
Additionally, it explored how integrating feedback analytics can support data-driven decision-making, enhance competency-based learning, and align assessment practices with broader educational objectives. The presentation offered a roadmap for institutions embracing this transformative shift.

title: DMU’s Prof. Naglaa Shehab Delivers Guest Lecture at Universitas 17 Agustus 1945 Jakarta
excerpt: Prof. Naglaa Shehab, Associate Dean- Academic Affairs and Professor in the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University, was invited as a guest speaker in a webinar hosted by Universitas 17 Agustus 1945 (UTA’45) in Jakarta, Indonesia. The event, held on June 21, 2025, was part of the ongoing academic exchange
content:
Prof. Naglaa Shehab, Associate Dean- Academic Affairs and Professor in the Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University, was invited as a guest speaker in a webinar hosted by Universitas 17 Agustus 1945 (UTA’45) in Jakarta, Indonesia. The event, held on June 21, 2025, was part of the ongoing academic exchange and collaboration under the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the two universities.

The topic of her guest lecture was titled “Development of New Technologies in the Phytochemistry in Herbal Medicines Using Nanotechnology”. The webinar attracted a wide audience of approximately 144 participants, including both faculty members and students from Indonesia. Prof. Naglaa explored the pivotal role of nanotechnology in enhancing herbal medicine formulation—emphasizing its contribution to improving bioavailability, refining pharmacokinetics, targeting cancer cells, and minimizing side effects.

The audience appreciated the informative and insightful session delivered by Prof. Naglaa, expressing strong interest in further academic and research collaborations between Dubai Medical University and UTA’45. Such webinars are excellent extracurricular opportunities for students, offering exposure to emerging technologies like nanoparticles and highlighting DMU’s growing capabilities in advanced pharmaceutical research and innovation.

content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an insightful Faculty Development Session titled “Effective Grant Writing”on Thursday, 29th May 2025. The session was attended by faculty members from across the university’s colleges and was delivered by Dr. Hanan Anbar, Associate Professor in the College of Pharmacy and Chair of the Institutional Review Board at DMU.
The session offered a comprehensive overview of grant writing essentials and shared practical strategies to help faculty successfully secure research funding. Key areas covered included:

  • Clearly defining research objectives and aligning them with funding priorities
  • Demonstrating the significance and potential impact of the proposed work
  • Structuring a persuasive, logically organized narrative
  • Developing realistic timelines and detailed budgets
  • Addressing reviewers’ expectations and avoiding common pitfalls

Dr. Hanan conducted this session following her participation in a specialized workshop organized by CLICKS on Thursday, 1st May 2025. She thoughtfully integrated both her own grant writing experience and the key takeaways from the workshop to empower DMU faculty in their future grant applications. This effort also supported the directives and guidance of Prof. Sherief Khalifa, DMU Vice Chancellor of Academic Affairs and Dean of the College of Pharmacy, in enhancing research productivity, securing competitive funding, building research capacity, and fostering a culture of scholarly excellence across the university.
Sincere appreciation to Dr. Hanan for sharing her experience and leading this impactful initiative.
Thanks to all faculty members who participated and contributed to the enriching discussions.
Gratitude to CLICKS for offering such a timely and valuable topic that supports DMU’s mission of advocating institutional research excellence.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Welcomes Its Newest Faculty Member: Dr. Naglaa Ashmawy
excerpt: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Naglaa Ashmawy, Associate Professor, Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy. Dr. Ashmawy brings with her a portfolio of academic, research, and leadership experience that is expected to contribute to advancing pharmacy education and research. Dr. Ashmawy earned her Ph.D. and
content:
Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Naglaa Ashmawy, Associate Professor, Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy. Dr. Ashmawy brings with her a portfolio of academic, research, and leadership experience that is expected to contribute to advancing pharmacy education and research.

Dr. Ashmawy earned her Ph.D. and M.Sc. in Pharmaceutical Sciences from Ain Shams University, Egypt, and has held previous academic and research positions at institutions in the UAE and Egypt. She previously served as Director of International Academic Programs and played a key role in Quality Assurance and Program evaluation.

A specialist in Natural Product Chemistry, Dr. Ashmawy’s research is focused on drug discovery from natural sources, with broad expertise in the extraction, isolation, and structural elucidation of secondary metabolites. She is highly skilled in advanced metabolomic profiling techniques such as HPLC, GC/MS, and LC/MS, and applies chemometric and multivariate analysis to gain insights into disease mechanisms and uncover novel therapeutic candidates.

At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Ashmawy is expected to lead the integration of Herbal, Complementary, and Alternative Medicine (CAM) into the curricula of the medical colleges through interprofessional education strategies. Her appointment aligns with the university’s vision to promote innovation and evidence-based practices in integrative medicine.

In addition to her academic responsibilities, Dr. Ashmawy will lead the development and innovation of the university’s Medicinal Garden and greenhouse, a key initiative aimed at supporting research, education, and community engagement in the field of herbal and integrative medicine. She will be responsible for managing research and academic activities related to the greenhouse, including the cultivation and study of medicinal plants, interdisciplinary research, and hands-on student training in natural products and traditional medicine.

Additionally, she will contribute to the university’s drug discovery research initiatives, particularly those involving AI-driven natural product research, and will work to foster strategic collaborations with international research centers and universities, expanding the university’s global research footprint.
With a strong track record of publications in peer-reviewed journals, international conference presentations, and ongoing collaborative projects, Dr. Ashmawy’s appointment marks a significant step toward strengthening Dubai Medical University’s academic excellence and research leadership in pharmaceutical sciences.

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) successfully conducted a faculty development session on May 21, 2025, titled “Enhancing Student Engagement and Learning Outcomes: A Showcase of Interactive Learning in Pharmacy Education.” The event, held in DMU Hall 205, was led by Dr. Rana Sammour, Assistant Professor at the College of Pharmacy, and was attended by faculty members from various colleges across the university.

The session focused on innovative, interactive teaching strategies aimed at enhancing student engagement beyond traditional lecture-based methods. Dr. Rana showcased practical, evidence-based approaches she has successfully integrated into her courses to promote active learning within the pharmacy curriculum. These methods contribute to creating a more dynamic and inclusive classroom environment and have been shown to significantly improve students’ academic performance, increase participation, and elevate overall satisfaction with the learning experience. Among the active learning techniques presented were:

  • Jigsaw Technique
  • Think-Pair-Share
  • Gallery Walk Technique
  • Hands-On Activities
  • Flipped Classroom
  • Inquiry-Based Learning
  • Real-World Scenarios

This initiative aligns with the vision of Prof. Sherief Khalifa, Vice Chancellor of Academic Affairs & Dean of the College of Pharmacy, who is a strong advocate for transforming education through interactive and student-centered teaching methods. Prof. Sherief has consistently encouraged faculty to adopt innovative pedagogies that not only enhance academic outcomes but also promote critical thinking and real-world problem-solving skills among students.

The event served as a platform for knowledge sharing and professional growth, reflecting DMU’s commitment to academic excellence and continuous faculty development. Faculty participants praised the session for its relevance, practical insights, and alignment with the university’s strategic goals in advancing health professions education.

title: Productive visit of Dubai Medical University and Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi on Advancing Pharmacy Education and Practice in the UAE
excerpt: On April 29, Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted a dynamic and forward-thinking meeting with Prof. Sherief Khalifa, Vice Chancellor Academic Affairs and Dean, College of Pharmacy at DMU, along with Prof. Mirza R. Baig, Associate Dean of Clinical Affairs, in collaboration with the pharmacy team at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi (CCAD), including Dr. Saad Sultan
content:
On April 29, Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted a dynamic and forward-thinking meeting with Prof. Sherief Khalifa, Vice Chancellor Academic Affairs and Dean, College of Pharmacy at DMU, along with Prof. Mirza R. Baig, Associate Dean of Clinical Affairs, in collaboration with the pharmacy team at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi (CCAD), including Dr. Saad Sultan – Executive Director of Pharmacy, CCAD, Dr. Rania El-Lababidi – Senior Manager, Pharmacy Education and Training, Dr. Mohammed Siddique, Dr. Shuaib Mahomed, Dr. Antoine Cherfan, Dr. Hisham, Dr. Layla Yousify, and other distinguished pharmacists.

The meeting focused on strengthening institutional partnerships to elevate the pharmacy profession in the UAE through advanced training and international collaboration. A key highlight was the in-depth discussion on the evolving soft skills required for pharmacists to thrive in the UAE’s healthcare environment, as well as the substantive updates to the national pharmacy curriculum. Prof. Sherief also shared insights into the enhanced clinical training model being introduced at DMU, particularly the newly designed four-month clinical rotations tailored for BPharm graduates.

We are pleased to share that CCAD has agreed to host undergraduate pharmacy students from DMU for clinical rotations—marking a significant step forward in bridging academic excellence with clinical practice. content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) is the first educational institution in the United Arab Emirates specializing in medicine and pharmacy, with over 40 years of experience in higher education. Established with a pioneering vision, the university is dedicated to investing in women’s education, empowering them, and strengthening their role in healthcare and medical sciences.

Since its inception, DMU has been committed to delivering high-quality academic programs accredited internationally, in collaboration with prestigious global universities. Its focus on scientific excellence, practical training, and comprehensive healthcare education is supported by an advanced learning environment that fosters innovation and student success.

Today, the university proudly hosts leading colleges in Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing. The recently accredited Bachelor of Nursing program marks a strategic milestone aligned with the UAE National Agenda, aiming to expand the pool of qualified healthcare professionals to meet the sector’s growing needs and enhance the quality and sustainability of healthcare services.

DMU offers modern academic programs with internationally aligned curricula, cutting-edge laboratories, and technologies, including AI and virtual reality simulation labs. With a distinguished and experienced faculty, DMU stands out as the academic destination of choice for ambitious female students seeking excellence in healthcare.

In collaboration with the Nafis program, DMU offers 100% scholarships for UAE nationals in the Pharmacy and Nursing programs to support the development of national talent. Additionally, the university provides scholarships of up to 40% for students of all nationalities—making world-class medical education more accessible—while maintaining some of the most affordable tuition rates in the UAE.

Prospective female students and their parents are warmly invited to visit the university campus from Monday to Friday, between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM. Visitors can explore academic programs, meet the faculty, tour the laboratories and facilities, and benefit from same-day registration.

title: DMU College of Pharmacy Welcomes Its Newest Faculty Member: Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) is delighted to welcome Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini as its newest faculty member. Dr. El Ouweini joins as a Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist. Dr. El Ouweini brings to DMU a wealth of academic, clinical, and research experience. He completed
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) is delighted to welcome Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini as its newest faculty member. Dr. El Ouweini joins as a Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist.

Dr. El Ouweini brings to DMU a wealth of academic, clinical, and research experience. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship in clinical pharmacy research with a focus on critical care—a joint program between Gulf Medical University and Washington State University. He is also a Board-Certified Pharmacotherapy Specialist (BCPS), completed ASHP-accredited PGY-1 Pharmacy Practice Residency, a certified clinical preceptor, and a licensed clinical pharmacist with credentials from the UAE, Lebanon, and the USA.

Prior to joining DMU, Dr. El Ouweini served as Clinical Lecturer and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist at Gulf Medical University and Thumbay University Hospital between 2021-2025, and this was preceded by serving as a Clinical Lecturer and Clinical Pharmacist at Lebanese American University Medical Center between 2020-2021. His expertise spans critical care pharmacotherapy, cardiology, infectious diseases, and nephrology, and he has delivered over 50 invited presentations and workshops across international conferences. Dr. El Ouweini has authored multiple peer-reviewed publications in the field of pharmacy practice and critical care.

Beyond his academic and clinical achievements, Dr. El Ouweini plays a leading role in the IVPN-Network, where he serves as Chair of the IVPN-Webinars Organizing Committee and Leader of the IVPN-Critical Care Listserv—advancing global collaboration and continuous professional development among pharmacists. He is an active member in several international pharmacy organizations, including ACCP, ASHP, and the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM), where he serves as the Social Media and Digital Lead for the Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapy Section. Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini

The College of Pharmacy is excited to have Dr. El Ouweini on board and looks forward to his contributions in advancing clinical education, interdisciplinary practice, and research excellence at DMU.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Bassam Atallah
excerpt: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Bassam Atallah, Pharm.D., M.S., BCPS, FHFSA, FCCP, as Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs, College of Pharmacy. Dr. Atallah brings with him a portfolio of academic, clinical, research, and leadership experience that has advanced pharmacy education and practice in the UAE and
content:
Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Bassam Atallah, Pharm.D., M.S., BCPS, FHFSA, FCCP, as Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs, College of Pharmacy. Dr. Atallah brings with him a portfolio of academic, clinical, research, and leadership experience that has advanced pharmacy education and practice in the UAE and the region for over a decade.

Dr. Atallah has most recently served as a Senior Pharmacotherapy Specialist at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Clinical Associate Professor at Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine where he contributed to some “Clinical firsts” in the UAE including the development of innovative pharmacist-led clinics. Prior to moving to the UAE, he served in the faculty of Clinical Pharmacy at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences (KSAU-HS) in Riyadh. He has also served different roles as subject matter expert with the Department of Health Abu Dhabi and Ministry of Education Commission for Academic Accreditation. In addition to his contributions to many other academic institutions in the UAE and beyond, thus bringing a wealth of international, regional and local academic experience.

Dr Atallah received his PharmD from Bernard J. Dunn School of Pharmacy in Virginia and completed an ASHP accredited post graduate residency at Winchester Medical Center in Virginia, USA. He was awarded the “Graduate of the Last Decade” award by his alma mater. Dr Atallah is a fellow of the Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA) and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP). He has many publications and presentations at national and international conferences. He was awarded the 2021 ACCP Cardiology PRN international award. His research interests are in various aspects of cardiovascular pharmacotherapy with a focus on antithrombotic therapy, heart failure and hyperlipidemia. At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Atallah is expected to lead the experiential clinical education components of the PharmD and Master’s programs. This is in addition to contributing to curriculum development, didactic education and clinical faculty development. In addition to his academic responsibilities, Dr. Atallah will lead the development of pharmacy clinical services at affiliated sites including at Dubai Medical University Hospital. His appointment will set the stage for future development of postgraduate training programs in clinical pharmacy at affiliated sites. With a strong track record of practice, teaching and research, Dr. Atallah appointment marks a significant step toward strengthening Dubai Medical University’s academic and clinical excellence and innovation in contemporary pharmacy education.

title: Dubai Medical University Launches UAE’s First Herbal and Integrative Medicine Summer Internship
excerpt: Dubai Medical University (DMU) launches the UAE’s first Herbal and Integrative Medicine Summer Internship, an innovative program from July 1 to 29, 2025. This innovative initiative is tailored for DMU students from the Colleges of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing, offering them a unique opportunity to explore the intersection of traditional healing and modern scientific innovation.
content:
Dubai Medical University (DMU) launches the UAE’s first Herbal and Integrative Medicine Summer Internship, an innovative program from July 1 to 29, 2025. This innovative initiative is tailored for DMU students from the Colleges of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing, offering them a unique opportunity to explore the intersection of traditional healing and modern scientific innovation.

To introduce the program, Dr. Naglaa Ashmawy conducted a live webinar on May 27, 2025. The webinar welcomed students from all three colleges, offering them a detailed tour of the internship’s themes and outcomes. Dr. Ashmawy emphasized that integrative medicine is becoming essential in modern healthcare, and this program equips medical students with the skills to combine traditional and evidence-based practices, broadening their approach to patient care.

The internship features four key thematic modules, each representing a vital area of integrative healthcare.

  • AI-Powered Complementary Medicine
    Exploring how artificial intelligence transforms herbal therapies through predictive tools and personalized treatment design.
  • Herbal Medicine: From Lab to Market
    Focusing on safe preparation, phytochemical understanding, and commercialization of evidence-based herbal products.
  • Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)
    Introducing the history, core therapies, and acupuncture techniques of TCM, with relevance to modern integrative care.
  • Foundations of Homeopathy
    Covering key principles, remedy formulation, and clinical case management within homeopathic practice.

One of the most distinctive aspects of the internship is its hands-on component, hosted at the DMU Green House. Here, students will work collaboratively to develop their ownAI-driven herbal products. These products will be presented to a panel of researchers and industry professionals, offering students a chance to receive expert feedback and refine their innovations. This experiential learning approach not only enhances their research and development skills but also fosters creativity and critical thinking.

Students who successfully complete the internship will be awarded a certificate from Dubai Medical University, recognizing their efforts and achievements in this program.

Dr. Naglaa Ashmawy, the internship course leader, commented: “This internship offers an innovative approach to learning by integrating traditional natural therapies with modern technology, including applications of artificial intelligence. It allows students to explore the evolving role of integrative medicine within a structured and research-informed framework.”

Prof. Sherief Khalifa emphasized the importance of strengthening collaborations between DMU and AHD to elevate the pharmacy profession, and he introduced international collaborative programs initiated by DMU, offering certified courses for selected pharmacists all over UAE and extended to AHD pharmacist. Discussions also focused on enhancing the training opportunities for DMU students at AHD and setting clear parameters regarding the number of students accepted for clinical training. Prof. Sherief expressed his deep appreciation for the exceptional quality of training provided by AHD, while Dr. Firas Alani commended Prof. Sherief’s visionary leadership in advancing healthcare education. Both sides agreed to further organize training programs in a more structured and professional manner to benefit both preceptors and students. Prof. Sherief sincerely thanked the AHD team for their warm hospitality and commitment to academic excellence.

title: Dubai Medical University: Full scholarships for UAE nationals in pharmacy and nursing programs
excerpt: Dubai Medical University is the first specialized educational institution in medicine and pharmacy in the United Arab Emirates, with over 40 years of experience in higher education. content:
Dubai Medical University is the first specialized educational institution in medicine and pharmacy in the United Arab Emirates, with over 40 years of experience in higher education. It was launched with a solid vision to invest in women’s education, empower them, and enhance their role in healthcare and medical sciences.

Since its founding, the university has been committed to providing high-quality academic programs with international accreditation and agreements with prestigious international universities, with a focus on academic excellence, practical training, and integrated healthcare, within an advanced educational environment that supports female students and provides them with opportunities for excellence and innovation.

Today, the university includes leading colleges in the fields of medicine, pharmacy, and nursing. The newly accredited nursing program is a strategic step in line with the UAE’s National Agenda, which aims to increase the number of qualified healthcare professionals to meet the growing needs of the healthcare sector and enhance the quality and sustainability of healthcare services.

The university boasts modern educational programs and teaching plans that align with global requirements, advanced laboratories and technologies focused on artificial intelligence and virtual reality labs, and a highly qualified and experienced faculty, making it a preferred academic destination for ambitious female students seeking excellence in healthcare.

The university offers 100% full scholarships to UAE nationals in the Pharmacy and Nursing programs, as part of its cooperation with the NAFES program, to support the development of national cadres in the healthcare sector.

The university also offers scholarships of up to 40%, enhancing access to high-quality medical education for all female students, at prices considered among the lowest in the country despite the advanced level of education.

To learn more about the programs and specializations, the university invites interested female students and their parents to visit the university’s headquarters in Dubai – Muhaisnah 1, from Monday to Friday, from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, to meet with faculty members and visit the university’s laboratories and facilities.

title: Dubai Medical University Welcomes Dr. Nalan Utku – A Global Leader in Immunology and Biotech Innovation
excerpt: On April 10, 2025, Dubai Medical University had the honor of hosting Dr. Nalan Utku, a distinguished Professor of Immunology at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin and internationally recognized biotech entrepreneur and innovator. Dr. Utku, a clinician-scientist with over two decades of experience in translational medicine, drug development, and regulatory affairs, has led groundbreaking work in
content:
On April 10, 2025, Dubai Medical University had the honor of hosting Dr. Nalan Utku, a distinguished Professor of Immunology at Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin and internationally recognized biotech entrepreneur and innovator.

Dr. Utku, a clinician-scientist with over two decades of experience in translational medicine, drug development, and regulatory affairs, has led groundbreaking work in oncology and autoimmune disease therapeutics. With multiple board positions, global patents, and published scientific contributions, she continues to be a key advisor to biopharmaceutical companies and venture capitalists across Europe and the US.

The visit began with a warm welcome extended by the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Sherief Khalifa, and the Deans, who introduced Dr. Utku to the DMU community and highlighted the significance of her visit to the University’s academic and research missions.
At DMU, she delivered two inspiring sessions. The first session for the DMU Students’ Career Session entitled “Overcoming Barriers – Becoming a Biotech Entrepreneur.” Students were deeply inspired as Dr. Utku shared her personal journey from her days as a medical student in Germany, through her research fellowship at Harvard Medical School, to becoming a biotech entrepreneur and scientific leader.

The second session for the DMU Faculty Research Seminar entitled “The Magic of Innovation – Transforming Knowledge into New Medicine.” Faculty members were highly motivated by her transformation of cutting-edge research into impactful therapies, leading to the development of over 30 patents in cancer and immune therapies. Her insights into translational medicine and academic entrepreneurship sparked exciting conversations about future research directions at DMU.

Following the sessions, Prof. Sherief Khalifa, along with members of the research team, accompanied Dr. Utku on a tour of DMU’s research facilities, showcasing the university’s ongoing initiatives and future aspirations in medical innovation.

title: Dubai students to get unprecedented access to top Indian universities like AIIMS, IIMA
excerpt: Students in Dubai will soon have access to top Indian universities like All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Indian Institute of Management (IIM) and Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), thanks to agreements signed during the first India visit of Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai. A deal
content:
Students in Dubai will soon have access to top Indian universities like All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Indian Institute of Management (IIM) and Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), thanks to agreements signed during the first India visit of Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai.

A deal was signed between Dubai Medical University (DMU) and the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) — one of the South Asian country’s top medical institutes — which gives students from DMU an opportunity to have an exchange programme in India.

The cooperation agreement, signed by Yahya Saeed Lootah, Vice Chairman of the Board of DMU, and Ahamadulla Shariff, Head of the Department of Anatomy at AIIMS, aims to strengthen academic and research collaboration.

According to Dr Shariff, the program will begin this year. “Initially, there will be some posting of DMCG students for a short time as observers, along with our students, at AIMS Delhi,” he told Khaleej Times. “Based on the requirement, some of our professors may come over for a short time as visiting faculty.”

Sheikh Hamdan’s two-day visit to the country, which came at the invite of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi saw several landmark agreements being signed, strengthening cooperation between both countries significantly.

“This is a great opportunity for our students,” said Denis Lefrancois, advisor to the chairman of S.S. Lootah group. “With the history of the AIIMS, all of their great experience, skills, facilities that they have, the number of patients that they see, the number of students that go through the institution, it is so going to be a great experience for our students.”

The AIIMS is a group of public medical universities in India. The oldest one was established in 1956 in New Delhi and currently there are 20 operational universities, with at least three more expected in the coming years. Considered one of the finest medical universities in India, AIIMS collectively takes in over 2,000 students every year.

Key areas of collaboration include joint research in priority fields such as infectious diseases, metabolic disorders, and climate change, and the development of global health initiatives. The agreement also provides a framework for the exchange of academic materials and research publications. The agreement also covers cooperation with AIIMS in areas related to AI research, development, and digital transformation in medical education and healthcare.

title: Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Marks the Successful Conclusion of the Preceptor Certificate Program in Collaboration with AACP and ACPE
excerpt: The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University is pleased to share that the fourth and final session of the Preceptor Certificate Program took place on January 12th, 2025. The full-day in-person session, titled “Taking Precepting to Another Level Through Case-Based Application,” provided participants with the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they had gained during
content:
The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University is pleased to share that the fourth and final session of the Preceptor Certificate Program took place on January 12th, 2025.

The full-day in-person session, titled “Taking Precepting to Another Level Through Case-Based Application,” provided participants with the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they had gained during the previous preparatory sessions. Throughout the day, 28 preceptors from 11 institutions worked collaboratively in small groups, tackling complex case scenarios that addressed real-world preceptor-learner challenges.

We were honored to have Dr. Craig D. Cox from Texas Tech University and Dr. Bassam Atallah from Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi as our speakers and facilitators for this session.

This program spanned four sessions in total. The journey began in September 2024 with the first session, “Start of Preceptor Journey – Self Discovery,” delivered by:

  • Dr. Craig D. Cox (Professor, Regional Dean, and Division Head – Medicine, Texas Tech University HSC Jerry H Hodge School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Kate Newman (Associate Professor & Director of Experiential Education, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Bassam Atallah (Clinical Associate Professor, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine).

The second session, held in October 2024, was titled “Start of Rotation – Learner/Site Preparation” and was delivered by:

  • Dr. Suzanne Larson (Director, Experiential Education, Midwestern University College of Pharmacy, Glendale, AZ Campus)
  • Dr. Megan Kaun (Director of Experiential Education, The University of Toledo, College of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences)
  • Dr. Nicole Gebran Connell, PharmD, BCPS, SQIL(HMS) (Senior Specialist Pharmacist – Clinical Pharmacy Lead, Dubai Health).

The third session, held in November 2024, focused on “The Feedback Experience: One Step at a Time” and was delievered by:

  • Dr. Angela Brownfield (Director of Experiential Learning & IPPE Coordinator, Clinical Professor, University of Missouri Kansas City (UMKC) School of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Rucha Bond (Clinical Professor, Pharmacy Practice Division, Assistant Dean for Experiential Education, The University of Texas at Austin, College of Pharmacy)
  • Dr. Sahar Elnajjar (Lecturer and Clinical Preceptor, College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University).

At the conclusion of the final session, preceptors were awarded Certificates of Program Completion, recognizing their dedication to enhancing their preceptorship skills.

We would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to all the instructors who contributed to delivering this program and to the the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) and to the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) for their collaboration and support.

This program’s success serves as the foundation for many more initiatives to come. We are excited to continue offering similar programs in the future, further developing our preceptors and contributing to the growth of pharmacy education and practice, both in the UAE and beyond!

Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with ACPE and AACP, Co-Organizes the Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University, in collaboration with the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy (AACP) proudly co-organized the 8th Regional Pharmacy Faculty Development Workshop on January 10-11, 2025.

The workshop brought together pharmacy education leaders from 24 colleges across the region, representing countries such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Libya, Iraq, Lebanon, Jordan, and all pharmacy colleges in the UAE.

The event welcomed approximately 12 deans of pharmacy colleges and esteemed faculty members, creating a vibrant platform for knowledge exchange, networking, and enhancing best practices in pharmacy education.

Key topics addressed during the workshop included:

– Best Practices in Experiential Education and Preceptor Development.
– Competency-Based Assessment, Grading and Skills Assessment.
-Artificial Intelligence in Pharmacy Education and Use by Academic Staff.

This two-day event provided an exceptional opportunity to strengthen collaboration among pharmacy colleges across the region, fostering innovation and excellence in teaching and learning.

As co-organizers, the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University expresses its sincere appreciation to all participants, including deans, faculty members, and representatives, for their active involvement and invaluable contributions, which made the workshop a success.

title: Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy Students Mark World Antimicrobial Awareness Week

content: The Community Engagement Unit of Dubai Pharmacy College and the DPC-IVPN students club, in collaboration Aster Pharmacy, hosted an awareness event at Aster Pharmacy, Mirdif City Center. Themed “World Antimicrobial Awareness Week: Educate. Advocate. Act now,” the event aimed to educate the public on rational use of antibiotics and proper hand hygiene. The event featured interactive activities to engage the community (i.e. customers of Aster Pharmacy, patients of the attached clinic), emphasizing the critical role individuals play in combating antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Volunteers shared essential information about antibiotics, including their appropriate use, common side effects, and the risks associated with misuse. Educational games, such as a crossword puzzle testing knowledge of antibiotics, added a fun and engaging element to the learning experience. One of the highlights of the event was a live demonstration of proper hand hygiene techniques, reinforcing the importance of infection prevention. Open discussions provided attendees with opportunities to ask questions and deepen their understanding of AMR and safe antibiotic practices.

title: Dubai Pharmacy College partners with American Pharmacists Association
