content:
On Monday January 6, 2025, a delegation from the American Pharmacists Association (APhA): Daniel Zlott Senior Vice President, Education & Business Development and Michael Rouse Senior Director, Global Initiatives entered signed an agreement with Dubai Pharmacy College (DPC). The agreement aims to advance the scope of practice of Pharmacy in the UAE to include immunization. APhA will train faculty, licensed pharmacists and students of DPC to become certified immunizers by APhA. The immunization training course will become part of the study plan for the Pharmacy degree program at DPC.

Dean Khalifa commented: “We are excited about our partnership with APhA and we are hoping that our initiatives with APhA will be contagious to all colleges of pharmacy in the UAE and the region. We believe that it is time to make use of the pharmacists’ workforce that has been underutilized for decades.”

During the visit, students explored AIIMS’s world-class clinical, research, and academic facilities, gaining valuable insights into diverse healthcare systems and innovative medical practices.

Upon their return, students presented their learnings to the Saeed Ahmed Lootah Charity Foundation (SALCF) Board of Trustees, reflecting DMU’s commitment to academic excellence and international collaboration.

This experience not only enriched their medical education but also strengthened DMU’s position as a globally connected institution preparing future healthcare leaders.

content:
As part of Dubai Medical University’s ongoing commitment to strengthening student engagement and enhancing governance participation, DMU successfully conducted an online Leadership and Guidance Training Session on 26 March 2024 for student representatives, including batch leaders and Student Union members.

This virtual session, designed to support and empower student leaders, focused on building essential leadership competencies and deepening students’ understanding of their roles within DMU’s governance structure.

During the training, participants engaged in interactive discussions and presentations covering key areas such as:

  • Leadership and teamwork
  • Effective communication skills
  • Roles and responsibilities within committees and governance bodies
  • Understanding decision-making structures at DMU

Through real-time activities and collaborative exercises, student representatives explored what leadership means to them, reflected on shared responsibilities, and gained clarity on how they can effectively contribute to improving student life and academic processes.

This initiative ensures that student leaders are well-equipped to engage confidently, ethically, and responsibly in committee work. It also helps them understand the broader ethical, legal, and societal context surrounding their roles—ultimately enhancing the quality, integrity, and impact of student participation within DMU’s committee system.

DMU remains committed to fostering a strong student voice and providing continuous development opportunities that build leadership capacity across the student community.

On Thursday, February 13, 2025, students from Dubai Medical University, College of Pharmacy actively engaged in the SEE Global Sustainability Summit roundtable discussion, held at The SEE Institute, Dubai.

Under the supervision of Dr. Rana Sammour, students Huda Al Nauimi and Sheikha Al Saffar took part in insightful discussions on sustainability and its impact on the UAE, highlighting the crucial role of youth in driving innovation for a more sustainable future.

The students contributed their innovative ideas to the conversation, emphasizing ways to support their community and country through sustainable initiatives. They also had the opportunity to collaborate with The SEE Institute team, exploring potential future partnerships to further advance sustainability efforts.

We are proud of our students for their dedication to environmental responsibility and sustainable development and look forward to seeing their contributions make a lasting impact!
